author: Eden Fineday
title: Help us keep the syilx Okanagan beat strong
content:
At the bottom of kɬúsx̌nítkʷ (Okanagan Lake) in snpink’tn (Penticton) on Aug. 26, community members gather and pray for the health of the land and for those affected by wildfires this summer.

Photo by Aaron Hemens


This story was reprinted from our newsletter. Subscribe for updates

here

 and learn more about our Okanagan campaign

here

.


The Okanagan was the very first community IndigiNews committed to covering.


When we launched in 2020, we made a promise to report on syilx Okanagan communities week after week with a consistency that shows our care and respect for the peoples and their territories. 


For the past four years, that promise has been kept by our reporter in the region, Aaron Hemens.


Today, his work is at risk.


Aaron on the ground in April 2024, reporting on a cultural burn.

Photo by Aaron Hemens


The funding that supported Aaron’s incredible reporting has ended. Without new support, IndigiNews will no longer be able to provide the same quality of dedicated storytelling we’ve offered in syilx Okanagan communities. 


Our goal

is to raise 

$35,000

 from our community of IndigiNews readers to keep Aaron covering the Okanagan. If we can reach our goal, we’ll be able to keep Aaron on the Okanagan beat for another full year — ensuring his vital reporting continues without interruption.


Keep the syilx Okanagan beat strong


We need to raise

$35,000

 to keep Aaron Hemens reporting from syilx Okanagan territory.


Help sustain independent, Indigenous-led local journalism.


Donate today


Aaron, a settler of mixed Filipino and European heritage, approaches his work with IndigiNews by centering the communities he’s reporting on. He believes journalism should be done in a good way — through building relationships that centre community protocol and accountability. 


As a man of colour, Aaron is very aware of what it means to be overlooked, misrepresented, and excluded in news media and beyond. This knowledge inspires him to show up at community gatherings, council meetings and court hearings to sensitively document the conversations that rarely make national headlines but nevertheless inform them.


nkwancinem Kim Montgomery dances at the Similkameen powwow arbour grounds on July 23, after being honoured for her 20 years of service with the Okanagan Nation Alliance.

 Photo by Aaron Hemens


This trust wasn’t built overnight. It took years of showing up for the people of the Okanagan. 


Across “Canada,” local journalism is disappearing. News deserts are spreading, hitting Indigenous communities particularly hard. As a result, important decisions are going undocumented, local histories are getting left unwritten, and people are less and less able to hold powerful institutions accountable. 


Stories disappear and, with them, access to the beating hearts of entire communities. 


At IndigiNews, we believe all communities deserve reporters who know the people they serve — not only during moments of crisis.


That’s why

we’re asking for your help

.


Community members exit a canoe after arriving in Penticton on July 30. The canoe was carved by Herman Edward, who participated in the original journey in 2001.

Photo by Aaron Hemens


As a registered Canadian charity, every eligible donation receives a charitable tax receipt. Whether you become a dependable monthly

 Firekeeper

 or make a one-time gift, your support directly sustains independent Indigenous journalism.


Every dollar protects the relationships IndigiNews has created — relationships that cannot simply be replaced.


If you’ve ever read one of Aaron’s stories, shared our reporting, or believe Indigenous communities deserve devoted local journalism, please consider making a gift today.


Together, we can ensure the Okanagan continues to have the journalism it deserves.


$35,000 Goal


Donate

Help us keep the syilx Okanagan beat strong

Indiginews

title: US Government Designates Host of NoBlogs.org a "Global Terrorist"
content:
On August 26, 2026, the United States government

classified

 the Italian collective Autistici/Inventati as a “Specially Designated Global Terrorist,” citing the collective’s “far-left” politics to justify the designation. They announced similar designations of the British group Palestine Action and the transnational Palestinian movement Masar Badil in the same statement.


Founded in 2001, Autistici/Inventati is a volunteer-run provider of privacy-oriented email, websites, mailing lists, blogs, and communications tools for users who prefer not to rely on corporate platforms. According to the US State Department, Autistici/Inventati hosts “roughly 16,000 mailboxes, 1,500 websites, 5,500 mailing lists, and 10,000 ‘blogs’ on its custom-built platform.”


Autistici/Inventati explain their values and goals in their

manifesto

:


We believe that communication must be free—and for free—and, therefore, universally accessible.


We try to accomplish all this by offering internet services (web sites, e-mail, mailing lists, chats, blogs, newsletters, and more) using our best skills and knowledge to defend both individuals or groups sharing our same aims or ideals. […]


We believe that media and communication should not be the exclusive domain of information professionals. We believe in the value of self-management: this is why we have no sponsors or funding of any kind, apart from voluntary donations from those who believe that our project is important and must survive. None of us earns a cent from this project (in fact, quite the opposite).


Many

book fairs

, radio programs, and other cultural projects rely on the Autistici/Inventati platform

noblogs.org

 for website hosting. According to one

anti-fascist research group

, “Some of the most well-known NoBlogs sites belong to researchers who solely report on far-right hate and radicalization, never doing anything aside from showing you what exists.” Such researchers helped to identify the fascists who participanted in the “Unite the Right” rally in 2017, during which one Neo-Nazi

murdered

 Heather Heyer in an

actual

 act of terrorism.


The US State Department is rationalizing this designation by alleging that Autistici/Inventati “provides encrypted tools and services to numerous violent far-left extremist groups,” including Portland-based Rose City Antifa. Their claim about Rose City Antifa seems to be

false

, however,

conflating

 Rose City Antifa with another project called Rose City Counterinfo.


On the basis of this error, the State Department rushed to

proclaim

 an alleged “Portland Antifa connection to Hamas” and “Iran’s IRGC” [Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps], with the sole justification being the allegation that an unnamed “extremist media group”—which they do not allege had any relationship to Rose City Antifa—had republished statements from Hamas and the IRGC on a website hosted by noblogs.org. This is representative of the dishonesty and erroneousness of the State Department press release as a whole.


When a military force carries out an attack on a village, the first thing they do is attempt to cut the communication lines that connect it to the outside world. We have to understand the attack on Autistici/Inventati the same way. Now that tech corporations from

Meta

 to the

platform formerly known as Twitter

 have showed that they are willing to ban whoever the US government instructs them to, the US government is going after groups that provide web services on a non-commercial basis.


Because there is no “domestic terrorist organization” designation in the United States, the Trump administration began its

criminalization

 of anti-fascists by

designating

 European anti-fascist groups as “terrorists.” They are targeting an Italian tech project for the same reason: they aim to put the pieces in place to criminalize domestic protesters by associating them with designated “Global Terrorist” groups.


According to the United States

Department of the Treasury

, starting on September 25, 2026, any transactions with Autistici/Inventati will be “prohibited
by the Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations.”

 from the Treasury stipulates:


Violations of US sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on US and foreign persons.

short statement

 about the designation:

title: Hospital Garrahan: persecución del gobierno contra Norma Lezana
content:
El ministro de Salud de la Nación, Mario Lugones, lanzó una campaña contra la Secretaria General de la Asociación de Profesionales y Técnicos (APyT) difundiendo que la misma habría sido despedida, lo cual nunca ocurrió. “Me quieren usar como cortina de humo para tapar los negociados turbios que estamos descubriendo”, declaró Lezana, refiriéndose al reciente informe que reveló que la cartera de Lugones desvió casi 60 mil millones de pesos del hospital Garrahan a inversiones financieras.


Norma Lezana. Foto: Maia Pauro


Con información de APyT, FM En Tránsito, Agencia FARCO y Periodismo de Izquierda.


En un acto en la puerta del Garrahan, tanto la propia Norma como su gremio aclararon que no recibió ninguna notificación formal de cese, que continúa ingresando a trabajar con normalidad y cuenta con la protección de sus fueros gremiales.


“Sin que haya mediado ninguna notificación formal a la licenciada Lezana, el ministro Mario Lugones en su cuenta de X, la página del Hospital Garrahan y en el medio A24 el periodista Eduardo Feinmann al aire, informaron y “festejaron” el “presunto despido de la emblemática profesional del hospital”, explicaron desde el sindicato, mediante un comunicado, en tanto que la misma Lezana lo desmintió también.


Lezana denunció que “es mentira que esté despedida. Primero, porque no fui notificada (y Lugones, Feinmann y la intervención lo anuncian como una “primicia”) y luego porque soy Secretaria General electa del sindicato que representa 24 profesiones del hospital y al conjunto de técnicos y trabajadores, y tengo protección gremial que sigue vigente, aunque Lugones y sus acólitos en el Garrahan crean que esto es una dictadura. No puede decidir ninguna cesantía, a pesar de no soportar que sea la única Secretaria General mujer, independiente y que no calla ante ninguna gestión”.


Foto: Maia Pauro


Lezana aseguró que “es evidente que están montando una cortina de humo atacándome a mí, para que no se sepa lo que estamos denunciando y empezamos a descubrir: contrataciones directas sin concurso, licitaciones millonarias sin rendición de cuentas de una empresa privada de seguridad o el uso de fondos por casi 60 mil millones de pesos del Garrahan en especulación financiera, mientras niegan la compra de prótesis y medicamentos para nuestros pacientes. No nos vamos a callar. No les tenemos miedo. Ninguna intervención autoritaria me va a sacar del Hospital”.


En este contexto, se realizó un acto este miércoles en la puerta del nosocomio, en defensa de Norma y del Hospital Garrahan.


Foto: Julieta Luna


Este ataque contra Lezana persigue un claro doble objetivo, plantearon desde el gremio. Por un lado, responde a una política de revanchismo del gobierno, que busca castigar a una de las referentes del histórico conflicto que el año pasado logró quebrar la pauta salarial oficial.


Al mismo tiempo, los trabajadores denunciaron que esta persecución, avalada por la dirección designada por Lugones, funciona como una cortina de humo para tapar graves irregularidades: contrataciones directas millonarias en seguridad privada y el desvío de casi 60 mil millones de pesos del presupuesto hacia la especulación financiera, todo mientras se niega la provisión de prótesis y medicamentos básicos para los pacientes.


Foto: Maia Pauro


Aquella lucha en el Garrahan demostró que es posible frenar las políticas de ajuste de Javier Milei mediante la más amplia unidad en la diversidad, la participación directa de las bases y la independencia política de todas las gestiones.


La plata de la salud de las infancias desviada a la bicicleta financiera


Un informe basado en documentos oficiales reveló que el Hospital Garrahan acumulaba más de 58 mil millones de pesos en inversiones financieras.


Escuchá el reporte de Sergio Lucarini, de Fm En Tránsito.


La Asociación de Profesionales y Técnicos del Hospital Garrahan (APyT) criticó al Ejecutivo por destinar fondos a la bicicleta financiera en lugar de volcar los recursos de forma directa a las necesidades urgentes y salarios del personal.


Voceros y cuentas oficiales del Gobierno intentaron desmentir la información, calificaron la noticia como falsa y aseguraron que se tergiversó la información contable y el desglose de los rubros del hospital.


Alejandro Lipovich, trabajador del Hospital Garrahan y secretario general de la Junta Interna de ATE, explicó en diálogo con

FM En Tránsito

: “Es algo similar a lo que sucedió el año pasado, a partir de distintos pedidos …

title: O que podemos aprender com a tragédia do Nepal?
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Ligando os pontos, enviada toda quinta-feira. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Ainda sob o impacto da devastadora avalanche e enchente de lama no Nepal, me pergunto o que poderia ter sido feito para evitar a perda de tantas vidas. Passados 12 dias do desastre, já são mais de mil mortes confirmadas e cerca de 3 mil pessoas ainda desaparecidas. Será que poderia ter havido alguma sirene ou uma mensagem por celular que avisasse a população sobre o perigo iminente?


Alguns

especialistas disseram

 que a velocidade do desprendimento do bloco de gelo e seu impacto no rio Trishuli, na fronteira com o Tibet, foi tão rápida que não haveria tempo para emitir um aviso de emergência. Mas, de acordo com reportagens publicadas até agora, ficamos sabendo que não existia um sistema de alerta preventivo na região atingida. Nesta semana,

a Reuters revelou

 que avanços em um monitoramento do estado das geleiras foram interrompidos pela resistência do governo da China em compartilhar dados com o Nepal.


O repórter Alec Luhn, que trabalha na revista britânica New Scientist, é um especialista em cobertura da criosfera (o nome dos ecossistemas congelados do nosso planeta). Em

um post, ele lembrou

 que um evento semelhante – o colapso de um glaciar – ocorreu na Suíça no ano passado, atingindo a vila de Blatten. Na ocasião, apenas uma pessoa morreu. Isso só foi possível porque um alerta emergencial foi emitido e as pessoas deixaram a cidade em tempo.


Com o aquecimento global, os glaciares em todo o mundo se tornaram muito mais instáveis. O gelo em ambientes montanhosos, como aquele onde ocorreu a avalanche, vai se afinando a cada ano. Na região afetada no Nepal, os verões dos dois anos anteriores tinham registrado as temperaturas mais altas na série histórica. Algumas destas geleiras demoraram milênios para serem formadas, aponta Luhn, mas poderão desaparecer apenas no período de uma vida humana.


No Brasil não temos geleiras, mas temos nossos próprios eventos extremos climáticos. A tragédia mais viva em nossa memória é a mega enchente

no Rio Grande do Sul

 em 2024. No estado, 440 mil pessoas ficaram desalojadas e 184 perderam a vida. Naquela ocasião, houve sim uma mobilização importante dos órgãos responsáveis. Alertas meteorológicos foram emitidos, a defesa civil entrou em ação. Mas a imprevisibilidade jogou um papel importante: a transformação de uma tempestade em um evento de alta intensidade ocorreu em pouco tempo e sem que pudesse ser detectado pelos sistemas de monitoramento.


Com isso, a lacuna que se tornou evidente no Rio Grande do Sul foi a falta de manutenção da infraestrutura existente e de investimentos para se adaptar aos novos tempos. Com a temperatura média global subindo mais do que 1,5ºC, eventos devastadores como esse são esperados. A adaptação, então, se torna a palavra do momento. Precisamos adaptar nossas casas ao calor e frio extremos. Precisamos pensar no suprimento de água e alimentos frente às secas e enchentes constantes. Precisamos de alertas de emergência climática, seja para nos salvar de uma tempestade ou de uma queimada destruidora.


A injustiça climática


Se com alertas a capacidade de resposta já é um desafio, sem eles os impactos se tornam ainda piores. É também uma questão de justiça social. Pois, como temos visto nas situações de emergência, os mais pobres se tornam ainda mais vulneráveis. São eles que perdem todas as suas economias em uma enchente ou deslizamento de terra. São eles quem têm menor chance de resistir aos impactos por estarem em zonas de risco.


Uma das

maiores tempestades já registradas

 em um dia no Brasil ocorreu em fevereiro de 2023 em São Sebastião, no litoral de São Paulo. Ela deixou evidente esta desigualdade dos impactos climáticos. Ali, após a queda de quase 800 mm de chuva em apenas algumas horas, 65 pessoas morreram em deslizamentos de terra. A maioria vivia em ocupações irregulares nas encostas da Serra do Mar. Como no Nepal, não houve sirenes ou alertas.


Mas é preciso reconhecer que tivemos avanços importantes nos últimos anos na implementação de sistemas de alertas preventivos. Em 2011, após a tragédia que afetou

as cidades serranas do Rio de Janeiro

, o governo da então presidente Dilma Rousseff deu um passo fundamental com a criação do Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais,

o Cemaden

. Este órgão público reúne …

author: anred
title: Lanzan campaña por el sobreseimiento de 19 manifestantes llevados a juicio por participar del «Jujeñazo»
content:
Represión en Jujuy ante el rechazo a la reforma constitucional – Foto: Guillermo Castro


A tres años del «Jujeñazo», 19 de sus protagonistas serán llevados a juicio en una causa que comenzará el 26 de octubre y se extenderá durante diez jornadas, hasta el 6 de noviembre. Organizaciones de derechos humanos, sindicales, sociales y políticas, comunidades originarias y personalidades lanzaron un llamamiento nacional para exigir su absolución y sobreseimiento y denunciar un nuevo avance de la criminalización de la protesta social. «No puede haber una Justicia para quienes lucharon y otra para quienes ejercían el poder y dieron órdenes ilegítimas», remarca el llamamiento, que reclama además investigar e imputar a los funcionarios implicados en la represión. «Abajo la reforma, arriba los salarios» fue la consigna que sintetizó el «Jujeñazo» de junio de 2023, una masiva movilización que reunió el reclamo de docentes y estatales por salarios con la defensa de los territorios de las comunidades originarias y el rechazo a la reforma constitucional impulsada por Gerardo Morales, y que tuvo como respuesta una brutal represión que dejó más de cien personas detenidas, numerosas heridas y manifestantes con gravísimas lesiones.

Por ANRed.


A tres años del «Jujeñazo», 19 de sus protagonistas serán llevados a juicio

, en una causa cuyo debate comenzará el próximo

lunes 26 de octubre y se extenderá durante diez jornadas, hasta el viernes 6 de noviembre

. Ante esta situación, organismos de derechos humanos, organizaciones sindicales, sociales y políticas, comunidades originarias y personalidades lanzaron un

 llamamiento nacional para exigir el sobreseimiento y la absolución

 de quienes son perseguidos judicialmente, y cuyo petitorio se puede

firmar aquí

.


La conssigna «

Abajo la reforma, arriba los salarios

» fue la consigna que sintetizó las jornadas de

junio de 2023

, cuando la

lucha de docentes y trabajadores estatales por salarios confluyó con la resistencia de las comunidades originarias en defensa de sus territorios y con el rechazo de organizaciones sindicales, sociales y políticas a la reforma constitucional impulsada por Gerardo Morales

. Según el llamamiento, aquella movilización «arrancó uno de los aumentos salariales más importantes para los estatales jujeños y puso en jaque al gobierno provincial».


Imagen: Originarios.ar


La respuesta del gobierno de Morales en ese momento fue una

fuerte represión,

recuerda el documento del llamamiento: «

una brutal represión, con detenidos, numerosos heridos y manifestantes que sufrieron gravísimas lesiones, entre ellas pérdida de visión. Mas de 100 detenciones que luego derivaron en libertades y sobreseimientos».

 Aquel año, organizaciones de derechos humanos y organismos antirrepresivos también documentaron

detenciones irregulares, el uso desproporcionado de la fuerza y lesiones graves

 durante aquellos operativos.


La persecución judicial, sin embargo, continuó después de la represión porque, tres años más tarde, 1

9 personas que participaron de aquellas protestas son llevadas hoy a juicio

. El proceso está atravesado, denuncian desde el llamamiento, por «

graves cuestionamientos de las defensas respecto del derecho de defensa, el debido proceso y la imparcialidad judicial»

. Además, se cuestiona el modo en que fue fijada la audiencia: «el 21 de agosto de 2026 fue rechazado el pedido de no fijar audiencia y apenas seis días después, con quejas en trámite, el 27 de agosto, se notificó un debate de enorme magnitud concentrado en diez jornadas».


«¿Cómo piensa Morales devolverle la vista a nuestros hermanos? ¿El objetivo es enceguecer a todo el pueblo de Jujuy?»


Mientras se acelera el proceso contra quienes participaron de la movilización, las organizaciones reclaman que la Justicia avance sobre quienes ordenaron la represión: «

seguimos reclamando que se investiguen las responsabilidades políticas y penales por la represión de junio de 2023

, que dejó manifestantes con gravísimas lesiones, y que

se avance también en la causa de Caspalá, donde se debate sobre el territorio de la Comunidad Originaria y la corrupción de los funcionarios del gobierno provincial»

. Así, la campaña por el sobreseimiento de quienes participaron de la pueblada del «Jujeñazo» vuelve así a inscribirse en una disputa más amplia por

el territorio, los recursos naturales y el derecho a protestar

.


Asimimos, el juicio que comenzará en octubre no es solamente el capítulo …

author: Darío Aranda
title: El Niño despertó: lluvias extremas y olas de calor para un planeta en crisis climática
content:
Por Silvia Oliviero Ghietto*


La Organización Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) emitió un comunicado en el que advirtió que el fenómeno climático El Niño, que ya está en marcha, puede alcanzar una intensidad mayor que la habitual. En Argentina, a partir de noviembre-diciembre, aumenta la posibilidad de que ocurran

eventos de precipitaciones extremas en la Cuenca del Plata

 (integrada por Corrientes, Misiones, Formosa, Santa Fe, Entre Ríos, Buenos Aires, Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires y Chaco)

y en el Noroeste de la Patagonia

.


El Niño continúa intensificándose de forma constante combinado con océanos globales excepcionalmente cálidos y la probabilidad de un dipolo positivo en el Océano Índico, lo que determina una

probabilidad

de casi el 100 por ciento

 de un evento “muy fuerte”

. Por lo tanto, se espera que domine los patrones climáticos globales durante la temporada 2026-2027, con

aumento de probabilidad de temperaturas superiores a lo normal

 en gran parte del mundo y con cambios significativos en los patrones de lluvia, segúnel

C

entro de Predicción Climática de la Administración Nacional Oceánica y Atmosférica de Estados Unidos.


Las proyecciones científicas actuales sugieren que este El Niño podría convertirse en un evento comparable con algunos de los episodios más impactantes de las últimas décadas superando incluso el ocurrido en 1998. Los eventos de El Niño suelen alcanzar su punto máximo hacia finales del año, con la máxima influencia que suele sentirse entre noviembre y febrero.


Vale la pena aclarar que la Organización Meteorológica Mundial y las Instituciones de Referencia Climática clasifican los eventos de la Oscilación El Niño-Sur (ENSO) como débiles, moderados, fuertes o muy fuertes. Por lo tanto, el término "súper El Niño" utilizado por los medios de comunicación no forma parte del sistema de clasificación operativo y oficial.


Infografía: Organización Meteorológica Mundial


¿Que sabemos del fenómeno del Niño?


El Niño y La Niña son fases opuestas de

un patrón climático natural

 conocido como la Oscilación El Niño-Sur (ENSO), que

implica fluctuaciones de las temperaturas oceánicas en el Pacífico ecuatorial central y oriental, junto con cambios en la atmósfera

 suprayacente. Cuando la “Circulación Walker” (un flujo masivo de aire de este a oeste impulsado por las diferencias de temperatura y presión entre los océanos cálido occidental y el frío del este) se modifica desplazándose hacia el este en dirección a Sudamérica y la temperatura oceánica supera los 0,5 °C, se declara El Niño.


La transición entre estas fases extremas suele ocurrir cada dos a siete años. Tanto El Niño como La Niña generalmente comienzan a desarrollarse entre marzo y junio y alcanzan su máxima intensidad entre noviembre y febrero.


El Niño se caracteriza por temperaturas superficiales oceánicas inusualmente cálidas en el Pacífico

 central y oriental.

El nombre proviene de pescadores y marineros peruanos que notaron una corriente cálida

, asociada a la reducción de capturas de pescado, y la llamaron El Niño (probablemente porque se hacía visible en torno a Navidad).


El Niño se predice mediante el monitoreo de las condiciones en el océano Pacífico tropical. A través de modelos climáticos, la comunidad científica puede estimar cómo puede evolucionar en los próximos meses y

predecir patrones climáticos con seis meses de anticipación

. Se basa en una red global de observaciones, incluidos satélites, buques de océano, barcos de investigación y medidas atmosféricas operadas por los Servicios Meteorológicos y Hidrológicos Nacionales y Organizaciones Internacionales.


Desde la década de 1980, el enfoque dominante para medir o identificar El Niño ha sido el uso del Índice Oceánico Niño (ONI), que calcula a lo largo de un promedio de tres meses la Anomalía de Temperatura Superficial del Mar en una región específica del Pacífico llamada región Niño. En los últimos años y con la presencia del calentamiento global, una métrica más reciente llamada Índice Relativo Oceánico Niño (RONI) ha ganado terreno. Este enfoque mide el calentamiento relativo, no solo el absoluto, ayudando a la comunidad científica a evaluar si un evento de calentamiento está impulsado por el ENSO o se debe principalmente al calentamiento global oceánico.


La OMM indica que, según las proyecciones de la Oficina Nacional de Administración Oceánica y Atmosférica (NOAA) de Estados Unidos y el Programa Copernicus de la Unión Europea,

author: A.N.A.
title: Sou a Anarquia!!!
content:
Nasci com a primeira revolta insubmissa, inquieta, desgrenhada. Construí a mim mesma desnuda, bela, irreverente. Desde meus ossos inermes partiu a primeira blasfêmia ao criador… Neguei-me a ser submetida, dirigida, apadrinhada. Transformei-me em apóstata, fui acusada de irreligiosidade. Fui condenada, mas minhas asas eram de fênix, e rapidamente abandonei as fogueiras e atravessei os oceanos… Vi jugos em todo lugar, dores e fome, discursos e lamentos, aprendi o desespero. Cavei com as unhas uma trincheira de sonhos e me embriaguei com esse bando de jovens loucos, poetas náufragos de volta à Espanha de trinta e seis… Olhei à esquerda, olhei à direita e vi rostos sujos escondidos atrás de limpos uniformes vertendo o sangue dos povos em nome da justiça, da dialética e outras quintessências enjoativas… E peguei a raiva e afiei-a e lancei raios contra os tronos, inimiga dos governos, inimiga das pátrias, inimiga da dor. Abraço o mundo, vivo e não imploro, amo e resisto suas tiranias.


Sou a Anarquia!!!


(Anônimo)

author: La Zarzamora
title: ENTREVISTA A AUTISTICI/INVENTATI. Contexto actual y cuidados colectivos
content:
Desde hace 25 años A/I se ha dedicado a proporcionar plataformas digitales seguras, a colectivos e individualidades. Su trabajo de autodefensa digital, consiste en dar servicios de cuentas de correos electrónicos y blogs, de manera anónima y segura. El objetivo de esta comunidad digital es «crear una infraestructura que pueda ayudar a la gente a protegerse», algo urgente y necesario en un contexto en el cual tus datos, información personal y cada movimiento que realizas bajo la lente de las big tech, se transforma en un producto rentable y vendible al mejor postor.

El 26 de agosto, Estados Unidos designó a Autistici/Inventati como una organización terrorista, generando múltiples reacciones de solidaridad, en el mundo del sofwer libre, la autonomía digital, en lxs usuarios y plataformas de código abierto.

Conversamos con lxs compañerxs de Autistici/Inventati, quienes nos contaron más sobre esta persecusión, lo que ha significado para ellxs y los cuidados necesarios, respecto a las cuentas que distribuyen a tantas colectividades.

Solidaridad con Autistici Inventati

author: CMI Argentina
title: Paola Ortiz en libertad
content:
El Tribunal Supremo de Justicia de Córdoba ordenó la liberación inmediata de la mujer cordobesa presa desde 2012 y condenada en 2015 a prisión perpetua por homicidio calificado por el vínculo tras sufrir un parto en avalancha sin asistencia médica en el que su bebé nació muerto. En 2024 se presentó un recurso de revisión de su condena, que finalmente le otorgó su libertad, luego de que el TSJ reconociera que la pena original careció de perspectiva de género, y no se tomó en cuenta la situación de precariedad en la que se encontraba Paola, ni la violencia física, sexual y económica que sufría.


Desde el Observatorio de las Violencias de Género “Ahora que sí nos ven” afirman que “Paola pasó 13 años presa injustamente, condenada por una justicia machista, misógina y revictimizante”: “Desde 2022, las abogadas Julia Luna y Rocío García Garro, siendo parte de la Guardia de Abogadas Feministas de Católicas por el Derecho a Decidir, tomaron su defensa legal. Fue en 2024 cuando presentaron un recurso de revisión de su condena, que finalmente le otorgó su libertad. En ese sentido, el TSJ reconoció que la condena original careció de perspectiva de género. Afirmaron que no se tomó en cuenta la situación de precariedad en la que se encontraba ni la violencia física, sexual y económica que sufría Paola. Por eso, redujo la pena al tiempo ya cumplido en detención: trece años, nueve meses y veintiséis días. Nos llena de alegría esta noticia, la cual es fruto de la lucha feminista que no retrocede pese a los obstáculos, y de la fortaleza de Paola, que durante estos años continuó luchando por su libertad. Las redes feministas son fundamentales para visibilizar y combatir las violencias que día a día sufrimos las mujeres cuando se trata de nuestros derechos reproductivos y sexuales. Paola no es el único caso, ya conocimos la historia de Belén, también presa injustamente tras haber sufrido un aborto espontáneo”.


“Lo seguimos gritando: ninguna emergencia obstétrica es delito. Queremos una justicia con perspectiva de género que no violente ni revictimice a las mujeres, que en situaciones de vulnerabilidad extrema, sufren este tipo de eventos obstétricos”, agregan desde el Observatorio.


En el mismo sentido, desde la Campaña Nacional por el Derecho al Aborto Legal, Seguro y Gratuito expresaron: “Paola Ortiz pasó más de 14 años en una condena injusta; la lucha feminista logró que el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Córdoba aplicara perspectiva de género y otorgue su libertad reconociendo que fue apresada injustamente como castigo por la vulnerabilidad y barreras de acceso a derechos ante una emergencia obstétrica, por lo cual fue condenada a prisión perpetua por homicidio agravado por el vínculo. Basta de criminalizar emergencias obstétricas. Nuestra lucha transforma vidas y sienta precedentes indispensables de justicia. Abrazamos a Paola, su familia y al equipo de abogadas que hizo posible este triunfo que celebramos”.

author: Jeniffer Mendonça
title: Apesar de proibição, Polymarket promove apostas sobre eleições brasileiras
content:
“Última hora: chances de Flávio vencer a eleição disparam”. A chamada, publicada em 31.ago.2026 no página do Polymarket no Instagram voltada ao público brasileiro, foi feita num carrossel com oito imagens, com uso de conteúdos da imprensa para dar contexto, memes sobre a situação e, no meio, o gráfico de previsões da empresa sobre quem deve ganhar as eleições presidenciais no Brasil.


No final, há um aviso de que as negociações de contratos envolvem riscos, não estão disponíveis em todas as jurisdições e são proibidas para menores de 18 anos. O post foi publicado em collab com a página @opoeteiro, que soma mais de 2,3 milhões de seguidores, e não há indicação se é uma publicidade.


Polymarket é um mercado de previsão baseado em criptomoedas. Na plataforma, os usuários podem apostar sobre o resultado de eventos futuros do mundo real, como eleições, esportes e até guerras e outros eventos geopolíticos. Está proibida de ofertar e divulgar seviços no Brasil desde 24.abr.


Post no Instagram da @polymarketbrasil (agora @polymarketportugues) do dia 31.ago.2026


Esse é um dos posts mais explícitos realizado pelo Polymarket, apesar de a empresa estar proibida de ofertar e divulgar o serviço no Brasil desde 24.abr. 


Mas não é o único. Até 24.ago, o

Núcleo

 levantou 103 publicações com referência às eleições brasileiras que seguiram o mesmo roteiro, sendo parte delas feitas em colaboração (ou marcação via arroba) com páginas de fofoca, de memes ou comentaristas de esportes e de influenciadores.


Há até referências a site vinculado a aliado de blogueiro bolsonarista e site que recebeu dinheiro de agência ligada ao Banco Master para ampliar alcance (leia mais abaixo).


Por que isso importa?


O parágrafo 7 do artigo 6º da Resolução nº 23.735/2024 do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral veda o uso de plataformas digitais que ofereçam ou prometam, gratuita ou mediante pagamento de qualquer valor, “bens, produtos ou propagandas vinculados a candidatas ou a candidatos ou a resultado do pleito eleitoral”. O descumprimento pode configurar crime eleitoral, como abuso de poder econômico e captação ilícita de votos.

A Secretaria de Prêmios e Apostas (SPA), vinculada ao Ministério da Fazenda, determinou o bloqueio do Polymarket e de outros 26 sites de mercados de previsão, por entender que elas não são intermediadoras de investimentos no mercado financeiro e operam com lógica de bets sem autorização.

A SPA solicitou à Anatel a notificação dos bloqueios aos domínios (www.polymarket.com, por exemplo). A pasta também pediu que as páginas nas redes sociais ficassem indisponíveis no Brasil, o que foi feito por meio do acordo de cooperação com o Conselho Digital do Brasil, organização que tem ao menos 10 big techs associadas, como Meta, Google, TikTok e Discord. A página @polymarket está inacessível para brasileiros no Instagram, mas a @polymarketbrasil segue ativa e acessível na mesma plataforma. Por outro lado, o X não integra a entidade e a página principal do Polymarket também está disponível.


A FSB Comunicação, uma das maiores agências de assessoria de imprensa do Brasil, passou a atender o Polymarket neste ano e confirmou ao

Núcleo

 que a página @polymarketbrasil pertence à empresa.


Coincidentemente, logo após os questionamentos da reportagem, a página mudou o nome de usuário para @polymarketportugues na quarta-feira (2.set.2026). 


A assessoria não respondeu objetivamente aos questionamentos da reportagem sobre a operação da página, a relação com sites e outros perfis no Instagram nem sobre os conteúdos publicados.


Em nota, afirmou apenas que o Polymarket não tem equipe no Brasil, apenas prestadores de serviços pontuais e que a empresa “não apoia candidatos, partidos ou correntes ideológicas, não adota posicionamento editorial sobre eleições”. Disse que não vai comentar sobre “parcerias, campanhas, influenciadores e conteúdos específicos”, mas “reforça seu compromisso com práticas de comunicação transparentes e responsáveis” (leia a íntegra ao final do texto).


Pelos dados do Instagram, a página foi criada em 2021 e mudou de nome de usuário agora pela terceira vez, mas não há detalhes sobre quais foram os outros dois nomes anteriores. Em 2025, a página fez apenas quatro publicações (três em maio e uma em junho) em que uma criadora de conteúdo aparece em vídeos para falar sobre acontecimentos relacionados ao time de futebol do Corinthians. author: Andrés
title: Contra el extractivismo y el despojo territorial, las Warmis marchan al Congreso
content:
Este jueves al mediodía, mujeres de pueblos originarios de Jujuy se movilizan desde Plaza Miserere hacia el Congreso de la Nación para exigir el cese del saqueo minero. Por ANRed.


Las Warmis del Kollasuyu marcharán durante la mañana del jueves 03 de septiembre por la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. Provenientes de la Puna, la Quebrada y los Valles jujeños, las mujeres originarias trasladan su reclamo para presentar un petitorio formal ante el Congreso de la Nación, frente a la falta de respuestas por parte de la Dirección Provincial de Minería, la Dirección de Recursos Hídricos y el Ministerio de Ambiente de Jujuy, tras la Caminata de Mujeres del 2025.


Tal como adelantaron en su comunicado a la prensa, bajo el lema “Caminatas de Mujeres en defensa de la Pachamama 2026”, las voceras comunitarias exponen en esta jornada la contaminación que afecta a la Laguna de Pozuelos por el impacto de la actividad minera. “Exigimos el cese de la contaminación de nuestros territorios y el respeto a nuestros derechos como Pueblos Originarios”, señalaron en el documento.


Iniciada el 3 de agosto en Rinconada (Jujuy), la movilización al Congreso marca el cierre de la «Segunda Caminata de Warmis». Tras recorrer unos 2.000 kilómetros a pie durante todo el mes, con una reciente escala en Rosario, las manifestantes trasladan sus demandas a Buenos Aires. Denuncian la contaminación de la Laguna de Pozuelos y exigen la intervención de las autoridades nacionales ante la falta de respuestas del gobierno provincial.


Apuntan específicamente contra los daños generados por la Mina Pan de Azúcar, la Mina Pirquitas y la Mina Chinchillas. A este escenario se le suma la amenaza de desalojo que pesa sobre decenas de comunidades de sus tierras ancestrales debido al avance de pedimentos mineros a lo largo de toda la cuenca.


Las organizaciones exponen la violación del derecho a la Consulta Previa, Libre e Informada, consagrado en el Convenio 169 de la OIT, así como el incumplimiento del Acuerdo de Escazú (Ley 27.566) en materia de acceso a la información y justicia ambiental.


A través del petitorio que entregarán, las comunidades interpelan directamente al Poder Legislativo. Quieren: “saber si las comunidades originarias somos tratadas verdaderamente como sujetos de derecho colectivo» Y además, sostienen que: «cuestionamos el favorecimiento del extractivismo por encima del bienestar de las comunidades”.


La postura de las defensoras de la tierra es clara, y así lo dieron a conocer en su comunicado a los medios: «Las mujeres de la Puna, Quebrada y Valles no permitiremos que continúe la fragmentación de nuestras comunidades ni la destrucción de nuestros territorios ancestrales. Exigimos el derecho a permanecer y desarrollarnos en paz en nuestra tierra».

author: Shan Kenshin Ecaldre
title: Southern Tagalog communities call for justice on IHL anniversary
content:
Photo courtesy of Karapatan-Southern Tagalog

My grandchild was traumatized because he saw how soldiers killed his father.

LOS BAÑOS, Laguna — During the 77th anniversary of International Humanitarian Law (IHL), victims of rights violations, indigenous peoples, and human rights defenders gathered at the University of the Philippines Los Baños on August 28 to expose the continuing impact of militarization on Southern Tagalog communities.

Organized by Karapatan-Southern Tagalog and allied organizations, the human rights forum titled “Panaghoy at Pag-asa: Documenting Truth, Demanding Justice,” provided a venue for survivors and affected communities to share testimonies of militarization, displacement, land grabbing, and state repression.

The event brought together Dumagat and Mangyan Indigenous Peoples, peasant communities, rights defenders, and supporters from various sectors. Their stories, though rooted in different struggles, showed the impact of militarization and impunity on marginalized communities.

Among those who spoke was Narcisa Dela Cruz, a Dumagat resident of Tanay, Rizal and the mother of Randy Dela Cruz and aunt of Puroy Dela Cruz, both of whom were killed during the Bloody Sunday operations in March 2021.

Dela Cruz recounted how military presence continues to dominate life in their community years after the killings. “Our barangay remains under tight military surveillance,” she said. “Whenever we return home, soldiers are constantly watching us. They accuse us of being connected with leftist groups.”

“I am not afraid because I have done nothing wrong,” she said. “All I want is justice for the death of my son.”

The emotional burden of the killings, she said, goes beyond the victims. Her grandchild witnessed Randy’s death and continues to suffer from trauma.

“I cannot accept that my son was killed by the military,” she said. “My grandchild was traumatized because he saw how soldiers killed his father.”

Dela Cruz also spoke of the continued military deployment in their community, stressing that soldiers would interrogate residents and would insist that they are linked to the New People’s Army (NPA).

Noli Tamisan of the Mangyan-Iraya from Sitio Malatabako, Occidental Mindoro recounted their efforts to defend a 32-hectare area that he said is part of their ancestral domain.

He said that the community erected a barricade in 2024 to stop Peaceland, a private entity, from taking over the land.

For a month, community members remained within the barricaded area. The standoff, however, was met with police and military intervention.

“Our struggle became more difficult because of arrests that violated our rights,” Tamisan said.

He said that several community members, including himself, were detained and charged with trespassing. “We continue to live in fear because military surveillance remains widespread in our area.”

Erlindo Baez, a human rights advocate from Batangas and one of the survivors of the Bloody Sunday raids, said that the roots of repression in his community can be traced to struggles over land.

Since 2010, farmers in San Juan, Batangas have experienced land grabbing and economic marginalization, he said.

“Faced with these conditions, we fought back and demanded justice,” Baez said. “As a result, our area became heavily militarized.”

Baez said that the consequences extended to his family. His son was arrested and charged with what he described as fabricated cases.

More than five years after Bloody Sunday, Baez said that he continues to seek justice for victims and accountability for those responsible.

The forum was also attended by Signe Poulsen, representative of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) Southeast Asia Regional Office.

Addressing survivors and victims’ families, Poulsen stressed the importance of documenting abuses and ensuring accountability.

“It takes great courage for people to speak about the most difficult days of their lives,” she said.

Poulsen said that the United Nations has long monitored the human rights situation in the Philippines and stressed that accountability remains essential to achieving peace.

“The experiences shared here need to be brought to the attention of the world,” she said. “We need accountability for human rights violations because accountability is essential to peace.”

Poulsen described the Bloody Sunday incident as a “one-sided attack” in which activists and human rights defenders were targeted …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Taitung Graft Probe Highlights Recurrent Issues of Rural Corruption
content:
ISSUES REGARDING local corruption are again in the news, with a number of pan-Blue Taitung city councilors questioned about the use of public funds to build a resort.

The resort, the Dongying International Resort, is linked to the family of Taitung County Council Speaker Wu Hsiu-hua. In May, independent city councillor Lin Tsan-tian raised during a county council meeting that public funds had been used to expand a road leading to the Dongying International Resort. Though the road was originally supposed to be three meters wide, it was expanded to nine meters wide. Reportedly, the road is also at least partly on state-owned land. For its part, Taitung authorities claimed the road was to benefit local farmers and prevent accidents, though no accidents had occurred on the road in the past decade.

What raised suspicion was that the discretionary funding of several city councilors was used on the road. Lin pointed to that while county councilors usually use discretionary funding to help repair roads or assist farmers to construct water tanks, they do not usually pool their discretionary funding on a road in this way.

In the wake of Lin’s questioning, a probe was launched. Seven city councilors have been questioned to date, six of whom are members of the KMT, and one of whom is a member of the People First Party. Wu was recently endorsed by Taichung mayor Lu Shiow-yen of the KMT in the upcoming elections.

Nevertheless, issues of corruption are far from unheard of in rural areas in Miaoli. Recently, KMT Legislative Caucus Leader Fu Kun-chi, who represents Hualien, came under scrutiny after former Financial Times journalist Kathrin Hille referenced widespread vote buying in Hualien during an interview on FTV.

Fu has long faced allegations of vote buying, not only in Hualien, but in the KMT Central Standing Committee election. Fu’s wife, Hsu Cheng-wei, is currently Hualien county magistrate, and she originally took up the post after Fu was arrested on corruption charges. Prior to his jailing, Fu divorced Hsu and named her deputy county commissioner to skirt nepotism laws, leading to a lawsuit against him over a fake divorce. Though Fu was previously kicked out of the KMT for his actions, he has since been welcomed back in because of his ability to win elections, and consequently risen to become KMT legislative caucus leader.

Other recent cases of high-profile corruption have also involved pan-Blue county magistrates. In January 2025, former Nantou county magistrate Lee Chao-ching, a former KMT member, was sentenced on charges totaling 656 years and four months in jail.

Charges facing Lee were mostly regarding kickbacks for reconstruction projects after Typhoon Morakot, which struck Taiwan in August 2009. Lee reportedly demanded 10% in kickbacks for reconstruction projects, which were passed to him in gift boxes of tea and fruit.

In December 2024, former Yilan county magistrate Lin Zi-miao was sentenced to 12.5 years in jail on charges of corruption. The charges against Lin date to 2022, when Lin came under scrutiny in connection to a development project on a 108-hectare plot of land in Luodong that was originally protected. However, the land was later rezoned for agricultural use in 2018, though residential building construction and public infrastructure development were allowed on the plot. The plot’s rezoning, as well as related land disputes, were seen as suggesting lawbreaking. This was quickly linked to Lin, seeing as the purchaser of the plot of land after its rezoning was Lin Shu-mei’s son. Lin Shu-mei, a former member of the National Assembly before its abolition, is Lin Zi-miao’s cousin and is a fellow member of the KMT.

Lin then came under scrutiny for checks worth over 100 million NT received by Lin or her family members from former KMT legislator Yang Chi-hsiung. Yang was known to have had a close relationship with Lin when he served as legislator, assisting Lin electorally. Likewise, several of Lin Zi-miao’s children worked in a mining company under Yang’s name.

Issues of local corruption continue to be commonplace in Taiwan, then. It is to be seen if charges stick in Taitung or, as with so many other cases, they simply bounce off.

author: Sanjiv Pandita
title: The Street Fighter, in Loving Memory of Apo Leong
content:
Editor’s Note:

 On Friday, 14 August 2026, Apo Leong, who had made enormous, decades-long contributions to Asia’s labour movement, passed away in Hong Kong.


Apo, who grew up in Macau and moved to Hong Kong as a teeanger, worked tirelessly as a labour reporter, organiser, campaigner and leader. He was a mentor and friend to a generation of labour activists in Hong Kong and across Asia.


For many years, Apo worked at the Hong Kong Christian Industrial Committee (HKCIC) with a focus on victims of industrial accidents, and led the Asia Monitor Resource Center (AMRC) as its first Asian Director until his retirement in 2008.


In his many roles over the decades, he built networks in Asia, developed collaborations with labour groups, and engaged deeply in initiatives strengthening grassroots movements on workplace health and safety. In his retirement, Apo continued to support the movement.


We spoke with Sanjiv Pandita, who had worked with Apo at AMRC since 2001 and succeeded Apo as AMRC’s executive director between 2008 and 2016. They collaborated closely on building the Asian Network for the Rights of Occupational and Environmental Victims (ANROEV) which unites workers across more than 16 countries to demand safe workplaces.


In this interview, Sanjiv shared his memories of Apo Leong as an dedicated activist, a mentor, a leader, and, in Apo’s own words, a street fighter.


Asian Labour Review (ALR): Thanks for doing this interview. We know you have known Apo Leong as a friend, colleague, and mentor for close to three decades, and worked closely with him. What are your first memories of Apo Leong?


Sanjiv Pandita (“Sanjiv”):

 The first time I met Apo was in Macau in 1999. I used to be based in Delhi, working on occupational health and safety. In 1999, I joined a conference in Macau. I met this really simple person. He was jovial and very welcoming, and that’s something that has stayed with me. Yet he was very forceful in how he structured his argument.


After the conference, we were having hotpot, and Apo was preparing the food for everyone. I said, “Hang on, I am not sure if this meat is cooked. He was laughing.” That was my first memory. Then we went out, and I saw a red Ferrari car. Apo said, “Oh, do you want to take a photo with that? I said, “Yes, why not? And Apo took out a camera and clicked a picture of me.


Then there was a job opening for a documentation officer at Asia Monitor Resource Center (AMRC), and I applied for it. I had an interview in Hong Kong and joined the organisation.


At that time, AMRC was located in a small flat, and every Thursday, we would have lunch in the office. After lunch, Apo got up and started cleaning the dishes. I thought, “Hang on, he’s the executive director of an organisation, and he’s cleaning the dishes?” That was not something I had seen in India. Apo came across as a very humble and down-to-earth person.


We would later observe another side of Apo. Apo would usually be very calm in meetings. But once he started talking about structural inequality and how we needed to fight it as a movement, you would see his passion. He looked like a very different person. That was his passion.


ALR: You worked with Apo for many years at AMRC. What was your day-to-day work with Apo like?


Sanjiv:

 On my first day in the office at AMRC, we went to a protest in the evening. Apo asked, “What are you doing? Let’s go! Let’s go! Let’s go! He did not tell us what was happening. This was Apo’s style. You had to guess. Then, suddenly, we were outside a hotel because there was union-busting happening there.


He would explain by doing things rather than telling you: this is what the Hong Kong movement looks like, and these are the people in the movement. He would take you to an action and introduce you to people in the movement. Apo would throw you into the water, and you would learn how to swim.


One of the characteristics of the AMRC, and much credit goes to Apo, is that it was very bottom-up and democratic. There was no hierarchy. The entire decision-making process was conducted through staff meetings. This was a highly collaborative process. He was not a director; he was a leader, but not a manager.


I remember in staff meetings, people could even shout at him. We could disagree and shout, and in the end, Apo was still my friend. There was no fear of Apo. We considered him to be our brother. He would look to what was good for a movement. He was not a good project manager. I believe …

author: groundxero
title: The Next Election May be Our Last
content:
Donald Trump is determined to subvert the midterms. All that can save us, if he succeeds, is a national strike.


 


CHRIS HEDGES


Aug 31, 2026


 


The Trump White House has put into place a series of mechanisms to fix or invalidate the midterm elections. Congress will not save us. The courts will not save us. Our only hope — should the election be rigged or stolen — is nationwide strikes. Our only hope is to cripple the machinery of commerce and government, although this militancy will be met with savage state repression.


 


Otherwise, we are doomed. There will be no exit.


 


If the measures advocated by the Trump administration are implemented, 

emergency powers

 will be invoked to assert unprecedented federal control over voting. Federal agents will seize election materials. They have already 

seized

 ballots from previous elections.


 


The U.S. Postal Service will only send ballots to those 

included

 on federally approved eligibility lists drawn from state voter rolls. These rolls, subject to citizenship checks, will 

deny

 election-mail services entirely in states that 

refuse

 the administration’s demands for voter data.


 


Trump-

backed

 mid-decade 

gerrymandering

 has already dismantled Democratic-held districts and created new ones for the Republican.


 


Federal ID and citizenship-document requirements will disenfranchise 

millions

 of eligible voters, including lower-income Americans who lack access to the required documents and married women whose current names do not match those on their citizenship records.


 


Federal troops and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) — with $113.5 billion in additional funding 

allocated

 by Congress through September 2029 — will be deployed to or near polling stations which have a traditional Democratic Party majority. Those branded as “anti-capitalist” and “anti-Christian” or charged with belonging to 

antifa

 will be intimidated or blocked from voting.


 


The Republican majority in the House — regardless of the vote — will use its authority to certify election results to retain power, gaming the Electoral College and refusing to seat newly elected members of the opposition.


 


Overseeing the massive election fraud will be 

loyalists

 seeded by the Trump administration across state and federal election offices.


 


Trump — who attempted to overturn the 2020 election results and said he would 

refuse

 to accept the outcome of the 2024 election if he lost — 

ruminates

 about defying the Constitution in order to serve a third term. He has also floated the idea of canceling the upcoming election, 

telling

 Reuters “when you think of it, we shouldn’t even have an election.”


 


When Volodymyr Zelensky — whose presidential term 

ended

 in May 2024 — informed Trump that elections would not be held in Ukraine because of the war, Trump

 

responded, “So you’re saying, during the war you can’t have elections…So, let me just say, three and a half years from now, so you mean if we happen to be in a war with somebody, no more elections? Oh, that’s good.”


 


Trump

 

told

 The New York Times in January he 

regretted

 not directing the National Guard to seize voting machines after the 2020 election. Trump not only wants to

 

abolish

 mail-in ballots – Democrats vote by mail in higher numbers than Republicans – but voting machines and tabulators which allow election boards to post results on election night.


 


Trump laid the groundwork for federal interference in his national address in July on election fraud, 

charging

 that the elections are dangerously exposed to “hacking, exploitation, and foreign interference.”


 


This assault has been decades in the making. It did not begin with Trump.


 


I warned about the Christian nationalist movement and its latent fascism in my book “

American Fascists: The Christian Right and the War on America

The only proper tasks for the federal government, they believe, are tax collection, war and domestic security.


 


These goals are laid out in numbing technical detail in

author: rti_admin
title: India’s Gen-Z Movement: Challenges Ahead for the Teachers and the Buddhist Way Forward
content:
The resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, Minister of Education, Government of India (a Gen-X person born between 1965–1980), has come as a shock, as it was considered impossible to get a resignation from any minister of the Narendra Modi-led NDA government from 2014 till now. However, the students of Gen-Z (born between 1997–2012, now in the age group 14–29) made it possible, along with the Millennials (born between 1981–1996), Gen-X, and Gen-Alpha (born between 2013–2020). The Gen-Z students would be mostly from class 10th onwards, and some may be working professionals as well. The protests (mostly) by Gen-Z have shown the other generations that they have accomplished something that other generations could not have achieved in the last 12 years (although the support of other generations cannot be neglected). The Gen-Z students would then have a new level of confidence when they go to their classes and interact with their teachers. However, without the right guidance to channel it properly, this surge of confidence can easily tip into an obdurate, impudent, and supercilious attitude, turning their outlook entirely quixotic. Therefore, the role of teachers, supervisors, universities, institutes, etc., would come into the picture, and they would have to face certain challenges. The challenges mentioned are not exhaustive; instead, they are suggestive.

The first challenge that universities/institutes (overall) and individual teachers as well would face is: Are the Gen-Z students going to listen (śravaṇa in Sanskrit—the first step of learning) to their teachers and universities? Are they going to follow the rules and regulations of the university/institute and maintain the decorum of the classes? Why I think this may be a challenge is because the Gen-Z students, with their creativity of language and presentation, have shut the mouths of many mainstream media channels and politicians, and have also astonished political scientists who never expected the occurrence of this nation-wide protest (if not in India, then at least not under the present government). These students have not been in the mood to listen to anything that has no bearing on the government’s accountability for the suicides of many NEET aspirants. This is understandable considering the seriousness of the issue. However, some videos have shown that students have hooted at the biased media channels, as they have been determined not to listen to anything from them.

The second challenge deals with humility and humbleness. Humility is an important aspect of learning. Learning results in humility (as said, vidyā dadāti vinayaṁ). Learning also results from humility—if I think that I am superior to others in terms of knowledge, how can I learn from others? I would then do whatever I think is fit according to ‘me’, even if that act disrespects someone. Are the Gen-Z students going to contemplate their continuous learning from life (manan in Sanskrit—the second step for learning), or would they feel supercilious? Are the Gen-Z students going to be in the disposition to learn from their teachers? Why I think this may be a challenge is because the Gen-Z students have already contemplated the inevitable consequences of the ruining of the country if the lacuna in education is not fixed. For this, they have raised their voice for their right to education, and thereby they have taught the world the peaceful management of crowds, connecting people, and leading a crowd. However, this same sense of achievement may let them feel that they know everything. It is also possible that they may not contemplate new learning, reflect deeply, or sharpen their arguments and creativity. Rather, they may take refuge in harsh and abusive language to assert their points, which has already been seen in the protests by some of the students. This aggression might block any novel and meaningful discoveries in their learning journey.

The third challenge is the continuity and culmination of the above two and deals with real-life experiences (nidhidhyāsana). The real-life experiences of unexpected events occur only when we listen to others and continuously contemplate them. Without that, we would continuously live in one set of habituated thinking caused by our external environments. But by continuously listening to others, like our well-wishers—teachers, parents, friends, etc.—and critics, we would be able to contemplate and improve our habituated practices. But without checks and balances …

title: Serok Barzanî pêşwaziyê li Berpirsê Nivîsîngeha Peywendiyên Yekîtiya Ewropayê kir
content:
Roja Şemiyê 22ê Tebaxa 2026an Serok Mesûd Barzanî pêşwaziyê li birêz Rado Botom, Berpirsê Nivîsîngeha Peywendiyên Yekîtiya Ewropayê li Herêma Kurdistanê kir. Di hevdîtinê de Berpirsê Nivîsîngeha Peywendiyên Yekîtiya Ewropayê li Herêma Kurdistanê ku bi boneya bidawîhatina erkên xwe û malavayîkirinê serdana Serok Barzanî kiribû, her wiha pîrozbahiyê li Serok Barzanî kir bi boneya wergirtina Nîşana Asta Bilind a Papayê Pîrozê Vatîkanê û, rola dîrokî ya Serok Barzanî di parastina mafê pêkhatan û kûrkirina kultura pêkvejiyan û hevgirtinê di navbera hemû pêkhatên neteweyî û olî yên Kurdistan û Iraqê de bilind nirxand. Her di wê hevdîtinê de Serok Barzanî spasiya Papayê Pîrozê Vatîkanê kir û tekez li ser wê yekê kir ku em serbilind in bi wê yekê ku kultura dewlemend a pêkvejiyan û hevgirtina di navbera ol û neteweyên cuda de ji me re maye û wê piştrastiyê jî da ku ew kultur dê parastî bimîne û kûrtir bibe. Her wiha destxweşiyê li erk û keda Berpirsê Nivîsîngeha Peywendiyên Yekîtiya Ewropayê kir di dema karê wî de li Herêma Kurdistanê û hêviya serkeftinê jê re xwest. author: Unknown
title: Family returning to home and land in Girê Spî attacked by gunmen
content:
The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR) said that a family returning to their home and land in the village of Bir Temeh, in Girê Spî, was attacked by armed men who had been cultivating their land. SOHR said that family members were tortured, injured and forcibly expelled from the area at gunpoint.


According to information reported by SOHR, the family went to their land and found that it was being cultivated by an armed group. The family was attacked when they asked the armed group to leave their land.


The armed men reportedly tortured and injured family members and verbally abused them.


SOHR reported that the attackers forced the family out of the area at gunpoint and threatened to kill them. The family was also threatened not to approach their homes or property again.

author: Aaron Ernest Cruz
title: Declining poverty stats far from reality amid flooding, high prices
content:
Urban groups protest for the right to livelihood and to hold Marcos Jr. accountable. (Photo by Aaron Ernest Cruz/Bulatlat)

Marcos Jr. administration relies on unrealistic standards defining who is poor.

MANILA – Did poverty decline in the country? For Kadamay, an alliance of the urban poor, Filipinos are still struggling every day to survive.

Last week, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported that poverty incidence in all regions declined from 2023 to 2025. Filipinos classified as poor are said to have dropped from 15.5 percent in 2023 to 9.7 percent in 2025, or from roughly 17.5 million to 11.1 million poor people.

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) said that this shows the impact of the Marcos administration’s poverty alleviation programs.

Kadamay stressed that the statistics do not represent the collective experience of the urban poor “where they suffer from high prices of electricity, food, commodities, and oil while earning low salaries.”

On August 28, Kadamay and other groups held a national day of accountability after parts of Luzon suffered from severe flooding following a series southwest monsoon rains.

“Where did the government get those statistics? Is the lower poverty threshold of 97 pesos [$1.56] per day enough for Filipinos? There’s no legitimate measure of poverty rather than the lived experience of urban poor communities who are starving due to lack of access to their basic needs,” Mimi Doringo, Kadamay secretary-general, said.

Despite the rains, the groups pushed through with the mobilization in Mendiola and denounced the Marcos Jr. administration for showcasing recent statistics despite lack of accountability to hold those who are implicated in the anomalous flood-control projects.

Elvira Hiangan, 62, said that she did not feel that their lives were better in the past years as prices of goods remain high. She said that her four children stopped their education due to financial constraints and lack of opportunity.

Hiangan is a housewife who also looks after her six grandchildren as some of her children are single-handedly raising their kids.

“The taxes we pay are so high, but his [Marcos Jr.] programs for the poor are not sustainable and just trap us further in poverty,” Hiangan told Bulatlat.

Hiangan’s husband who works as a construction worker is not paid enough to cover their basic needs. She said that they even skip meals because of her husband’s insufficient salary.

“He is only earning a salary ranging from P500 to P700 ($8 – $11.30). Due to rainy weather, he can’t go to work.”

Hiangan’s family also experienced severe flooding for many years living in Sitio Bakal, Barangay Silangan, Quezon City.

“We are having a hard time sleeping when it continuously rains at night because our area is easily flooded,” she said.

Hiangan is one of the many people living in urban areas who are affected by botched or ghost flood-control projects.

The Center for Women’s Resources (CWR) said that the government’s figures represent a serious distortion of the extent of poverty in the Philippines. “By relying on a poverty threshold that does not adequately reflect the real cost of living or the income required for families to meet their basic needs and live with dignity, the government effectively narrows the definition of who is considered poor. This makes poverty appear smaller on paper than it is in people’s everyday lives.”

The group said that there may be millions of Filipinos classified as non-poor because their income falls slightly higher than the official poverty threshold. But CWR said that they continue to struggle to afford adequate food, housing, healthcare, education and other basic needs.

“The government is celebrating how many people have crossed the poverty line, but it is not asking the more important question: What kind of life can a Filipino family actually afford after crossing that line?” CWR Executive Director Cham Perez said in a statement.

Ibon Foundation said that the Marcos Jr. administration relies on unrealistic standards defining who is poor because their methodology uses the least-cost basket. This means that they only use cheaper goods to compute whether a Filipino household can afford it. The non-food needs are not considered in the computation.

“Poverty reduction should not mean merely keeping people barely above a statistical line. The government must create the conditions for sustained and broad-based improvements in living …

author: Brian Hioe
title: Taiwan’s Eswatini Science Park Investment Not Likely to Entail Any Scrutiny of Human Rights
content:
THE TAIWANESE GOVERNMENT has proposed funding a science and technology park in Eswatini at a cost of 1 billion NT, the Taiwan Industrial Innovation Park. The science park would be to shore up relations in what is Taiwan’s sole remaining diplomatic ally in Africa, with the aim of expanding the footprint for Taiwanese businesses in Africa. President Lai Ching-te and Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung previously visited the site of the proposed science park during a visit to Eswatini earlier this year.

The visit to Eswatini by Lai took place after a planned trip by the Taiwanese president for King Mswati III’s 58th birthday and the 40th anniversary of his accession to the throne was abruptly canceled. Countries that Lai would have passed over on his flight to Eswatini, Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles revoked overflight permissions shortly before Lai was to set out. This was largely interpreted as China flexing its muscles in terms of its influence in Africa, with the Lai administration suggesting that China threatened to revoke debt cancellation for Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles if they did not comply.

Lai’s trip, then, took place with Lai abruptly traveling to Eswatini, then only announcing that he had arrived after the fact. Presumably, this was to minimize the space for China to react. Lai arrived in Eswatini by traveling on King Mswati III’s personal aircraft, a former China Airlines plane that was sold to the monarch in 2015. Lai later returned on the same aircraft, taking a winding route that tested the operational limits of the plane, but similar to the route taken by then-US Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi during her August 2022 trip to Taiwan.

Still, one notes that–as is broadly the case with Taiwan’s diplomatic relationship with Eswatini–there was little criticism of Eswatini’s record on human rights afterward. Eswatini is an absolute monarchy. The constitution was voided in 1973, and political parties were banned, as a result of which free and fair elections still do not take place in Eswatini today. Although Mswati agreed to constitutional changes in 2005, he retains his grip on power. Under Mswati III’s rule, life expectancy has halved in Eswatini since 2000.

Pro-democracy protests rocked Eswatini in the summer of 2021, with the public calling for the right to vote. In the violence that followed, 28 were shot, with demonstrators alleging that at least twenty were killed. Tear gas was used by police against demonstrators, and Internet services were suspended, with a curfew declared in major urban centers, in which buildings were burned during the turmoil, including Manzini and Mbabane, as well as the industrial center of Matsapha.

Much as occurred during Taiwan’s authoritarian period, Eswatini also sees the killing of dissidents. In 2023, opposition politician Thulani Maseko was killed by unknown gunmen in a shooting widely suspected of being ordered by the monarchy. Maseko was a human rights lawyer and public intellectual. At the time, Mswati III stated, “People should not shed tears and complain about mercenaries killing them,” implying that he had ordered the killing.

Nevertheless, after the demonstrations, Taiwan announced that it would be donating 637 million NT to the government for reconstruction–an act that makes it complicit in the government’s crackdown on the protests. Either way, Taiwan simply chose to act as though the protests had never occurred.

Indeed, in spite of its human rights violations, Taiwan has continued to blithely engage in trade relations with Eswatini. In May, the Lai administration was asked about the prospect of importing labor from Eswatini. Online claims were that Taiwan planned to import 1,000 workers from Eswatini after Lai’s trip, something that government officials denied as disinformation. For its part, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs denied that Eswatini is being considered as a source of imported labor. It instead claimed that emphasis has been placed on cultivating vocational talent in the manufacturing, tourism, energy, and infrastructure sectors, so that Eswatini workers can work in Taiwanese-owned businesses in the science park that is being built in Eswatini.

It is probable that such claims were an attempt to leverage recent backlash to the prospect of introducing Indian migrant workers, with a wave of online racism against the idea, claiming that Indian migrants would sexually assault Taiwanese women en masse. The Lai administration …

author: groundxero
title: When the Mountain Broke: Inside Nepal’s Deadliest Himalayan Flood
content:
The disaster exposed the extreme fragility of high-altitude Himalayan ecosystems under a shifting climate.


 


By

Madhab Pant


 


At roughly 8:30 AM on 26 August 2026, a wall of water, mud, ice, and massive boulders roared down the Lhende Khola into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems. The surge struck without local rainfall or warning sirens, catching border communities like Timure, mid-morning. Initial reports mistook the ground tremors for an earthquake, but satellite and seismic data later confirmed the real trigger: a high-altitude collapse of rock and ice near Langtang Lirung, on the Tibetan side, spanning nearly one square kilometer and generating a ground shock equivalent to a magnitude 5.2 quake. Plunging 1,200 vertical meters into the valley, the avalanche briefly dammed the Lhende River before rupturing, unleashing a debris-laden slurry that tore through Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Tanahun, and Chitwan.


 


Environmental Drivers and Hydrological Cascade


 


The disaster exposed the extreme fragility of high-altitude Himalayan ecosystems under a shifting climate. Rising temperatures and accelerating freeze-thaw cycles are steadily degrading permafrost and the cryogenic bonds that hold mountain bedrock together, priming slopes for collapse. This was not an isolated event: smaller glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) incidents in July 2025 had already weakened local topsoil and riverbank integrity.


 


The catastrophe unfolded in two stages. First, the avalanche formed a short-lived debris dam across the narrow Lhende Khola. Hydrostatic pressure built rapidly behind the ice-and-rock wall as glacial meltwater and river discharge backed up, until the barrier gave way. Second, the released surge raced downstream at speeds exceeding 75 km/h, scouring up topsoil, riverbed gravel, and boulders as it went and turning into a hyper-abrasive slurry that gouged riverbeds, stripped valley walls, and undercut mountain foundations across the Bhotekoshi, Trishuli, and Narayani corridors. Secondary barrier lakes are still forming along blocked upper tributaries, prompting fresh flood warnings downstream.


 


Human Toll and Structural Damage


 


According to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and the Nepal Police, the toll on life and infrastructure has been devastating. Confirmed deaths have surpassed 669, with victims swept as far as Chitwan (248), Nawalparasi East (158), and Paschim Nawalparasi (75); some remains were recovered up to 240 kilometres away in India’s Uttar Pradesh. Between 1,000 and 2,426 people remain missing, including 933 hydropower workers, dozens of security personnel from the Nepal Army, Police, and Armed Police Force, customs officers, residents, and over 500 foreign nationals mostly trekkers and Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims from more than 30 countries.


 


On the recovery front, between 3,700 and 4,400 survivors have been treated or evacuated, including nearly 200 workers pulled from flooded underground hydropower tunnels. Damages are now estimated to exceed NRs 200 billion. The flood destroyed more than 80 bridges (35+ motorable, 45+ suspension) and washed out 40 kilometers of the vital Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi trade corridor, halting overland commerce with China. Thirteen run-of-the-river hydropower plants including the 111 MW Rasuwagadhi and 60 MW Upper Trishuli 3A sustained direct structural damage, knocking hundreds of megawatts off the national grid.


 


Ecological Disruption and Human-Made Risk


 


Beyond the human and economic cost, the scouring wiped out aquatic habitats and macroinvertebrate populations across Langtang National Park and its buffer zones. Millions of tons of topsoil were stripped from mountain slopes, while heavy silt deposits degraded farmland further downstream. Environmental assessments warn that unstable debris left in the upper tributaries could form new barrier lakes, raising the risk of further outburst floods when the rains return.


 


Human activity in these narrow corridors amplified the destruction. Encroaching highway construction, constricted floodplains, and loose excavation muck from active building sites added extra material to the flood’s path. Once the surge hit, this debris and the narrowed riverbeds turned built infrastructure into secondary hazards that intensified the wave’s force.


 


Emergency Response and Cross-Border Cooperation


 


Nepal deployed over 15,000 security personnel …
