title: Casi 100 mil trabajadores industriales perdieron su empleo desde que gobierna Milei
content:
En el marco del Día de la Industria, que se conmemora hoy, y según el último relevamiento del Centro de Economía Política Argentina (CEPA), desde la asunción al gobierno de Javier Milei en diciembre de 2023 han cerrado más de 30.600 pequeñas y medianas empresas en todo el país.


A raíz del cierre de estas empresas, según

el reporte del CEPA

 se perdieron casi 100 mil puestos de trabajo.


En vísperas del Día de la Industria, presentamos el informe “La industria manufacturera a dos años y medio del gobierno de Milei”. Adelanto de conclusiones:


Evolución de los principales indicadores de la industria


La industria argentina atraviesa un marcado deterioro. En…

pic.twitter.com/OGt1f3JzEh


— Centro CEPA (@ctroCEPA)

September 1, 2026


En ese sentido y en declaraciones a Aire Libre, el empresario Ricardo Cicarelli, vicepresidente de la empresa productora de amortiguadores CIRUBON S.A, dijo que la balanza está inclinada a favor de las importaciones y que no favorece a la industria nacional.


Está difícil a nivel nacional, yo creo que hay cosas que se están haciendo mal, las normas no son claras, la balanza comercial está totalmente desnivelada para el lado de las cosas importadas y no realmente para lo que tiene que ser, que son sus fábricas nacionales.


Por último, Cicarelli cuestionó la falta de controles para productos importados: “¿Quién controla lo que trajeron de afuera, esa basura que trajeron de afuera? Porque yo tengo controles por todo lados. Este tipo sacó todos los controles de las importaciones, dejó que acá en tu casa se te meta cualquiera, que hagan lo que quieran, que traigan lo que quieran”.


Desde noviembre de 2023 hasta mayo de 2026, la industria argentina perdió exactamente 97.312 puestos de trabajo registrados en unidades productivas del sector manufacturero, lo que equivale a una caída del 8%. En el mismo plazo cerraron 4.020 establecimientos industriales con trabajadores registrados (una baja del 8,1%).

title: 1 Year After US Began Boat Bombing Campaign, Victims’ Families Demand Answers
content:
Two families from St. Lucia and Colombia believe their loved ones, both fishermen, were killed at sea by US airstrikes.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A year ago today, the United States bombed a small boat in the Caribbean, killing nine people on board. Two survivors clung to the wreckage for 45 minutes, reportedly waving for help, before a second “double-tap” strike killed them, too. President Trump posted a video of the first attack on social media, announcing that 11 terrorists had been killed in a military operation that would be called “Operation Southern Spear.” The second video, showing the killing of the survivors, has never been released. The bombings have continued for a year, killing at least 227 people in nearly 70 separate strikes. The Pentagon often accuses the boats it targets of narcotrafficking.

In a new documentary, the investigative team at Al Jazeera’s Fault Lines traveled to St. Lucia and Colombia to speak with two families who believe their loved ones, both fishermen, were killed at sea by U.S. airstrikes. “They describe it as a war. They describe these people as enemy combatants that are attacking America,” says Josh Rushing, a senior correspondent for Fault Lines who worked on the documentary. In reality, “it’s unclear, really, if the U.S. government knows who they’re killing … They’ve never named anyone in any of the strikes.”

“We had the ‘war on drugs,’ the ‘war on terror.’ This is kind of the worst of both,” says Rushing.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

President Trump posted a grainy video of the first strike on social media, announcing to the world that 11 terrorists had been killed in action. The administration has refused to release video of the second strike on survivors, known as a “double-tap” strike, but it’s been seen by some members of Congress. The bombings have continued for a year, killing more than 220 people across roughly 70 strikes. Last month, the campaign, dubbed “Operation Southern Sphere,” was officially retired, but following a brief hiatus, the bombings have resumed.

U.N. experts issued a statement Tuesday demanding an end to the attack, saying, quote, “International law does not permit governments to simply murder alleged criminals at sea, just as the police cannot summarily execute people on the street in United States territory.”

title: Malvinas: excombatientes y abogados ambientalistas fueron a la justicia federal contra la explotación petrolera
content:
El Centro de Excombatientes de Islas Malvinas de La Plata y la Asociación Argentina de Abogados/as Ambientalistas presentaron una acción preventiva de daño ambiental ante el Juzgado Federal de Río Grande, en Tierra del Fuego, para frenar el proyecto petrolero “Sea Lion” (León Marino) en la Cuenca Malvinas Norte.


El objetivo del reclamo judicial es detener las obras y movimientos sobre el lecho marino planificados por la británica Rockhopper Exploration y la israelí Navitas Petroleum; además de solicitar el bloqueo de operaciones financieras y notificar a bolsas internacionales como las de Londres y Tel Aviv.


Excombatientes argumentan que la extracción de crudo en la plataforma continental argentina carece de autorizaciones nacionales y pone en riesgo extremo el ecosistema del Atlántico Sur. En declaraciones a Radio Encuentro el referente de CECIM La Plata, Ernesto Alonso, dio más detalles.


Ellos están operando en el área de concepción de León Marino, donde están anunciando ya que posiblemente en el 2028 puedan empezar a extraer directamente petróleo.


Además detalló: “Estamos hablando de Vaca Muerta 2, con la posibilidad de sacar 120.000 barriles de petróleo raros, diarios, perdón. Cuestión que ese petróleo, estas empresas en forma unilateral, violando todas las resoluciones de Naciones Unidas por parte de Gran Bretaña y las leyes argentinas”.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: US Fatally Bombs Wedding in Iran, Killing 4, Including Children
content:
Bomb remnants suggest the strike was carried out with a weapon once advertised as the Navy’s “most accurate” missile.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The U.S. fatally bombed a wedding in southern Iran on Tuesday, killing at least four people, including children, prompting the U.S. to be referred to the International Criminal Court (ICC) for potential war crimes.

U.S. munitions struck a house in which a wedding ceremony was being held in the city of Kuhestak, located in Sirik County. The Iranian Red Crescent and local officials said that at least four people were killed, including two children: 4-year-old Amir Ali Karimi, 16-year-old Mohammad Malahi, 43-year-old Kolsoum Malahi, and 43-year-old Zarkhatoun Taheri, per Al Jazeera. At least 68 others were injured, reports say.

Iranian officials reported that the U.S. also hit other civilian sites in a flurry of strikes on southern Iran on Tuesday evening, including a civilian airport. The renewed attacks came after a pause in U.S. strikes, during which Trump administration officials pledged that further kinetic action would be unnecessary due to its new sweeping sanctions regime.

The Iranian Red Crescent Society, which helped provide emergency services after the strike, said the attack is a war crime that must be prosecuted in the Hague.

“Given the reported civilian character of the location as the venue of a family wedding ceremony, as well as the presence of civilians at the site, the incident raises serious concerns under international humanitarian law (IL) and warrants an independent, impartial, thorough, and effective investigation,” the group said in a letter to the ICC’s chief prosecutor on Wednesday.

Video of the aftermath of the strike shared by the Red Crescent shows a building in utter chaos. People are yelling as they scramble over piles of rubble scattered everywhere, inside and outside.

Wedding ceremonies are now targets! To the list of U.S. war crimes against civilian targets in Iran, you can now add wedding ceremonies, following schools, stadiums, and residential houses. This photo depicts the scene of the US airstrike in Sirik pic.twitter.com/CCLSMph0w5

“The U.S. military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC,” said U.S. Central Command spokesperson Tim Hawkins, in response to reports of the strike.

However, the missile apparently used in the strike has been advertised as the U.S. Navy’s “most accurate weapon.” From pictures of the weapons fragments left behind at the site, weapons identification expert Trevor Ball identified the attack as using components of Boeing’s Stand-Off Land Attack Missile-Expanded Response (SLAM-ER). In a press release about the weapon in 2005, Boeing bragged that, in a test, the SLAM-ER received target information mid-air, “changed its course and directly hit the target.”

The U.S. has a long, sordid history of attacking weddings. Early in the U.S.’s war on Afghanistan in 2002, the U.S. struck a house full of wedding guests, killing at least 30. Then, in 2008, a U.S. air strike killed 47 civilians as they were on their way to a wedding in the village of Wech Baghtu, in Afghanistan. The strike killed the bride.

Another wedding procession was a victim of President Barack Obama’s drone strike campaign in Yemen in December 2013, when the U.S. launched Hellfire missiles on a convoy that killed at least 12 civilians and apparently wounded the face of the bride.

In all, since 2001, the U.S. has struck at least eight wedding parties. Tuesday’s strike happened just a couple dozen miles away from the town of Minab, where the U.S. struck an elementary school on the first day of its war on Iran, killing 168 people, most of them children.

title: People of Kobanê march under the slogan “Bê ziman jiyan nabe”
content:
In protest at a decree by the Ministry of Education of the Syrian transitional government reducing Kurdish-language education to three lessons per week, thousands of people in Kobanê took to the streets on Wednesday. During the march from the Free Women’s Square to the Peace Square, demonstrators carried banners reading “Şêrîn û xweş e zimanê Kurdî” (Kurdish language is sweet and beautiful) and “Bê ziman jiyan nabe” (There is no life without language).


Addressing the crowd, Kurdish-language teacher Meryem Abid recalled that Kurdish citizens have been studying in their own language since the beginning of the revolution and that they had realized a long-held dream through the revolution. She said: “For 14 years, we have been studying in our own language, Kurdish. Now, with this decision, they want to reduce Kurdish to just three lessons and replace it with Arabic. We used to study in Arabic, and we will continue to study it, but Kurdish will remain the primary language. We have a rich language in every respect.”


Meryem Abid stressed that their language is a red line for them, continuing: “It is our very existence. We cannot live without our language. Our language is a red line for us: either death or education in our own language.”


Student Dilovan Elo said that studying in a language other than Kurdish was not an option for them. “I am in sixth grade, and I am Kurdish. I go to school, and I accept nothing other than my Kurdish identity. We have only one language, and that is Kurdish. We do not accept any language other than Kurdish,” Elo said.


Kurdish-language teacher Caklîn Şêx Xidor said that children are currently being forced to study in a language that is not their own and warned that this would negatively affect their psychological well-being. She said: “Thanks to the efforts of Meryem Amara and her comrades, we have reached this level in the development of our language. The Kurdish language is now taught everywhere. However, following the decree, another attempt at linguistic genocide is being made. This is unacceptable. A fundamental condition of integration is the recognition of the Kurdish language in the Syrian Constitution. If this decision is not changed, we will not open our schools.”


Şêx Yihya Goraxlî stated that Kurdish is the second language in Syria and said: “Our language has been preserved throughout history, and we will continue to protect it. We are Kurds; our language was created by Allah and is from the Holy Quran. Just three lessons a week are not enough for us. It should be Arabic that is limited to three lessons a week. We do not accept this decision here.”

title: Shengal People’s Council: No decision concerning our future can be made without our representatives
content:
Over the past few days, significant new developments have taken place concerning Shengal, the situation of the Yazidi community, and the status of its defense forces. Yesterday, an important meeting on the situation in Shengal was held in Baghdad, chaired by the head of the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office. Representatives of Iraqi intelligence, security, and administrative institutions, as well as a representative of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Office, were present at the meeting. Comprehensive discussions were held on the security and administrative situation in Shengal, the return of displaced Yazidis, and several other important issues.


In the meantime, the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) Command issued a written statement denying claims that 2,200 YBŞ fighters have joined the Iraqi army. At the same time, YBŞ announced that it is ready for negotiations with Iraq in line with Iraq’s sovereignty and the interests of Shengal.


Against the backdrop of these critical meetings, statements and warnings, the Shengal People’s Council also issued a written statement regarding yesterday’s meeting in Baghdad. The Council warned that no new decisions concerning the future of the region can be made without representatives of Shengal and emphasized that this situation has caused concern within the Yazidi community. Stating that democratic integration is the most appropriate path toward a solution, the Shengal People’s Council called on the Iraqi government to officially recognize Shengal’s defense forces, including the YBŞ-YJŞ and Êzîdxan Asayiş.

title: Hesekê and Zirgan: Our language is our identity
content:
Hundreds of people in Hesekê and Zirgan protested the decision by the Ministry of Education affiliated with Syria’s interim government to allocate only three hours per week to Kurdish-language instruction in schools. The protesters demanded that Kurdish be recognized as an official language of education and that the decision be revised.


Hesekê


At the protest organized under the leadership of the Teacher Training Institute, banners reading “Our language is our identity” were carried. Following a musical performance, the protest concluded with slogans emphasizing the importance of the Kurdish language.


Zirgan


Citizens marched from the Women’s Bakery to Martyr Dijwar Junction, where the demonstration turned into a rally. Ruha Hac Eli, a member of the Zirgan School Administration, said that three hours of classes per week was insufficient and that students would not be able to study middle and high school in their mother tongue. Hac Eli emphasized that Kurdish is not merely a means of communication, but also a fundamental element of Middle Eastern civilization.

author: The Canadian Press
title: Removing a nod to Indigenous Peoples from Alberta birthday note “glitch” fixed: Smith
content:
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith says she stepped in to fix a “glitch” that saw Indigenous Peoples erased from her official statement marking the province’s 121st birthday.


Within an hour of sending the Alberta Day statement on Tuesday, the government sent an updated version removing the sentence including Indigenous Peoples from its English version.


Smith said public servants made the move and that she urged them to revert to the original statement.


“I said, ‘why don’t you just put up the original one? I thought it was fine, and so I’m not exactly sure what happened with that glitch,” she told reporters in Calgary at an unrelated announcement.


“We’re just excited to be able to celebrate Alberta Day and all of the various cultures, and diaspora communities, including Indigenous Peoples, who have helped to build the province,” she said.


“We want to celebrate everyone.”


Nevertheless, the change had already drawn concern from critics amid tense relations between Smith’s United Conservative Party government and Indigenous communities before the upcoming referendum on Alberta separation.


The vote on Oct. 19 is to ask Albertans whether they want to remain a part of Canada or begin the process to hold a second, binding referendum on separating from the country.


Treaty 8 Sovereign First Nations Grand Chief Trevor Mercredi called the removal of Indigenous Peoples from Smith’s statement deeply troubling.


“Our Nations are not a footnote to Alberta’s story,” he said in a news release.


He added it’s especially concerning as Smith’s government is advancing separation-related initiatives and challenging the constitutional status of treaty rights and the duty to consult.


“At a time when First Nations people are facing increased hostility for standing up for Treaty, the government should be affirming our place and history prior to Alberta’s story, not deleting it,” said Mercredi.


The rewrite also drew heat from the Opposition NDP’s Jodi Calahoo Stonehouse, who is a Cree and Mohawk member of the legislature.


“You might be able to erase us from your statement, but you will never erase us off our land,” she said on social media.


Yonathan Sumamo, spokesperson for government communications and public engagement, said in an email that Smith’s second statement was issued by mistake and that her first statement, including the government’s recognition of Indigenous Peoples, stands.


“We apologize for this error and any confusion that it may have caused.”


As of Tuesday afternoon, Smith’s statement, published on social media, did not recognize Indigenous Peoples. The government’s website was updated with her initial statement including Indigenous Peoples.

title: ABD'li aktör George Clooney, ABD yönetimini eleştirdi: Beceriksiz insanlar tarafından yönetilen bir ülkede yaşamak kolay değil
content:
Fotoğraf: Michael Vlasaty/Wikimedia Commons CC BY 2.0

Roma – ABD’li aktör, yönetmen ve yapımcı George Clooney, ülkesinin "beceriksizler" tarafından yönetildiğini söyledi.

İtalya'da bu yıl 83'üncüsü düzenlenen Venedik Film Festivali'nin açılış töreninde "Yaşam Boyu Başarı Altın Aslan" ödülünü alacak Clooney, tören öncesinde basın mensuplarıyla bir araya geldi.

İsim vermeden ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'a yüklenen Clooney, "Beceriksiz insanlar tarafından yönetilen bir ülkede yaşamak kolay değil." dedi.

Clooney, tarihin talihsiz bir anında olduklarına inandığını belirterek, ABD'de başka zor zamanlardan geçtiklerini ve bunun da onlardan biri olduğunu söyledi.

Clooney, ABD'de kasım ayında yapılacak ara seçimlere işaret ederek, "Bu, kesinlikle bir değerlendirme anı olacak ve her şey yolunda giderse, daha normal bir duruma döneceğiz." diye konuştu.

83. Venedik Film Festivali, bu akşam Clooney'nin "Yaşam Boyu Başarı Altın Aslan" ödülü alacağı tören ve ana yarışma kategorisinde de yer alan İngiliz yönetmen Danny Boyle'un "INK" isimli filminin gösterimiyle başlayacak.

Festival, 12 Eylül'deki ödül töreniyle son bulacak.

title: Almanya'da Leipzig-Halle Havalimanı'ndaki İHA saldırısı girişiminde 2 şüpheli belirlendi
content:
Almanya'da Leipzig-Halle Havalimanı'nda 4 Ağustos'ta Ukrayna'ya ait bir kargo uçağına yönelik gerçekleştirildiği öne sürülen patlayıcı yüklü insansız hava aracı (İHA) saldırısı girişimiyle ilgili soruşturmada, Rusya ile bağlantılı olduğu iddia edilen 2 şüphelinin belirlendiği bildirildi.

Süddeutsche gazetesi ve kamu yayıncıları NDR (Kuzey Almanya Radyo TV Kurumu) ve WDR'nin (Batı Almanya Radyo TV Kurumu) televizyon kanallarının güvenlik kaynaklarına dayandırdığı haberlerine göre, Federal Başsavcılık soruşturmasında 2 kişinin saldırının planlanması ve gerçekleştirilmesiyle bağlantılı olduğu değerlendiriliyor.

Şüphelilerden birinin Rusya doğumlu ve Letonya pasaportuna sahip olduğu, diğerinin ise Rus pasaportu taşıyan Belarus vatandaşı olduğu belirtildi.

Habere göre, Letonya pasaportuna sahip Rusya doğumlu şüphelinin saldırının lojistik hazırlıklarından sorumlu olduğu ve İHA kullanımı konusunda eğitim verdiği değerlendiriliyor.

Şüphelinin temmuz sonunda Berlin Brandenburg Havalimanı (BER) üzerinden Almanya'ya geldiği, kiralık araçla Leipzig'e geçtiği ve saldırı girişiminden 2 gün sonra yine BER üzerinden Almanya'dan ayrıldığı ileri sürüldü.

Soruşturma kapsamında olay yerinde elde edilen DNA izlerinin ikinci şüpheliye ulaşılmasını sağladığı, bu izlerin patlayıcıyla doldurulduğu belirtilen bir İHA üzerindeki konserve kutusunun iç kısmında ve havalimanı yakınlarında bir ağaca yerleştirilen anten üzerinde bulunduğu kaydedildi.

DNA izlerinin Avrupa'daki veri tabanlarında yapılan karşılaştırmasında Litvanya ve Finlandiya'da eşleşmeler bulunduğu bildirildi.

Soruşturmacıların DNA bulguları üzerinden ulaştığı belirtilen, Rus pasaportu taşıyan Belaruslu ikinci şüphelinin, İtalya tarafından verilen turist vizesiyle Almanya'ya giriş yaptığı, vizenin nisan sonunda Minsk'teki İtalyan diplomatik temsilciliğince düzenlendiği öne sürüldü.

Alman hükümeti de Leipzig'deki olaydan Rusya'yı doğrudan sorumlu tutmuş ve bir dizi tedbir açıklamıştı.

Dışişleri Bakanı Johann Wadephul, Bonn'daki Rus Başkonsolosluğunun 18 Eylül itibarıyla kapatılacağını, Berlin'deki Rus Evi ile ilgili sözleşmenin feshedileceğini ve Rus vatandaşlarına yönelik giriş kontrollerini sıkılaştıracaklarını belirtmişti.

Leipzig-Halle Havalimanı'nda geçen ayki saldırı girişimine ilişkin belirlenen 2 şüpheliden birinin İtalya'dan aldığı turistik vizeyle Almanya'ya giriş yaptığına dair haberlerin ardından İtalya Başbakan Yardımcısı ve Dışişleri Bakanı Antonio Tajani'den bir açıklama geldi.

İrlanda'nın Wicklow kentindeki gayriresmi AB Dışişleri Bakanları Toplantısı'na katılan Tajani, burada yaptığı açıklamada, "Kontrol edeceğiz. Vize verilmesi için bir süreç var çünkü belirli şartların yerine getirilmesi gerekiyor. Eğer kişiler bu şartları karşılıyorsa ve bireyler hakkında 'uyarı' yoksa vize veriliyor. Neden vize verildiğini anlamaya çalışacağız." ifadelerini kullandı.

Leipzig-Halle Havalimanı'nda İHA bulunmuştu

Almanya'daki Leipzig-Halle Havalimanı'nda 4 Ağustos'ta Ukrayna'ya ait bir nakliye uçağının yakınında patlayıcı düzeneği içerdiği değerlendirilen İHA bulunmuştu.

ABD istihbaratı, bulunan patlayıcı yüklü İHA'nın özelliklerinin, Rus askeri istihbaratına özgü olduğunu iddia etmişti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Chris Walker
title: Mike Johnson Supports Max Miller, Calls Him “Great Member of Congress”
content:
Johnson minimized the allegations against Miller, saying he is facing “some issues in his personal life.”

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Earlier this week, Speaker of the House of Representatives Mike Johnson (R-Louisiana) gave accolades to Rep. Max Miller (R-Ohio), a member of his party who is running for reelection in this year’s midterms despite multiple allegations of abuse from his ex-wife and other women he’s dated.

On Monday, Johnson was asked by reporters about Miller as he was walking through the halls of Congress. The lawmaker, Johnson said, “has been a great member of Congress.”

Johnson also downplayed the allegations against Miller, saying he is merely facing “some issues in his personal life” that he is “working through.”

Asked Speaker Johnson if he supports GOP Rep. Max Miller’s reelection bid. “Yes,” he said. “He has been a great member of Congress. He has some issues in his personal life he's working through.” Says there’s an Ethics Committee probe and “we have to let due process play out.”… pic.twitter.com/1BePSMYEWc

Asked directly if he still supports Miller’s campaign, Johnson said, “I have supported Max Miller’s re-election.”

Perhaps recognizing that he needed to pare back his comments somewhat, Johnson noted that the “House ethics committee is looking into” the allegations about Miller’s conduct.

“We have to let due process play out,” he said.

Johnson’s comments are a more direct indication of his support for Miller than what he said about a month ago. In early August, when Miller was facing calls to drop out of the congressional race (including from members of his own party), Johnson claimed he was ignorant of the situation, stating at the time that he hadn’t discussed the matter with the Republican congressman.

“It’s not my business to get engaged in it,” Johnson added.

Miller’s ex-wife, Emily Moreno, has alleged that he physically abused her and their 2-year-old daughter. Moreno has alleged that he held a gun to her head, and that he once broke his daughter’s collarbone, among other incidents.

Following those allegations, other women from Miller’s past have come forward, stating that they, too, were abused by the Republican lawmaker while they were dating him. Miller denies all claims made against him.

Amid attempts to defend his character, Miller posted a link to photographs of his daughter on his social media — images that included a nude image of the child.

Although supported by the Speaker and other members of the GOP, several Republicans have called on Miller to drop out of the race, including his ex-father-in-law, Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio).

“If there are any basic standards of character required to hold elected office, Max Miller fails them,” Moreno said in a post on X last month. “I believe Max Miller needs to seek professional help to end the clear pattern of abuse he has left in his wake. I believe he should not be free to continue endangering others until he does.”

Despite calls for him to step aside, Miller stayed in the race, and a deadline for him to drop out has already passed. Miller has specifically cited President Donald Trump and the numerous allegations of sexual abuse made against him for his decision to continue running.

In 2016, Trump “stayed in the fight,” Miller said in August. “Because Americans see — and one of the qualities that they respect the most is somebody who is resilient.”

The scandal surrounding Miller could result in a Democratic victory this fall in Ohio’s 7th Congressional District, which is widely considered a Republican stronghold. Polling from early August indicates that his opponent, Brook Park City Council member Brian Poindexter, is leading Miller by 14 points. Notably, in 2024, Trump won the district by 11.1 points, and Miller himself won the district by 15 points.

author: Jennifer Smith
title: Sen. Ed Markey Prevails Against Primary Challenger Seth Moulton
content:
The successful incumbent, who turned 80 during the campaign, co-authored the Green New Deal and backs Medicare for All.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

U.S. Sen. Ed Markey cruised to a decisive victory in the Democratic primary against U.S. Rep. Seth Moulton, as voters soundly rejected the Salem congressman’s effort to turn the race into a referendum on Markey’s age.

In unofficial results on Tuesday night, Markey secured roughly 70 percent among Democratic primary voters to Moulton’s 30 percent.

It marked the second consecutive race in which Markey turned back a primary challenge from a younger member of the state’s congressional delegation. Six years ago, it was 39-year-old Joe Kennedy III who failed to make the case for generational change. This time, with Markey turning 80 during the heat of the primary campaign, it was the 47-year old Moulton who waged an ultimately losing bet that the senator had finally worn out his stay.

Moulton launched his campaign last October with a simple pitch — it was time to pass the torch.

Moulton, a Marine veteran who served four tours in Iraq, argued that it was time for a generational change in leadership and that he would bring fresh energy to the fight against President Trump and his agenda.

Markey pointed to his authorship of the Green New Deal, consistent progressive bona fides, and said he had never felt more energized about a campaign. He insisted repeatedly that it was not your age but the age of your ideas that was important, and then pointed to his long record of progressive policy battles.

Every public poll of the race showed Markey comfortably ahead.

After the candidates met for their first debate on July 8, the numbers barely wavered. A Suffolk University/Boston Globe poll found a majority of voters already leaning Markey by mid-August. A WBUR/UMass Amherst survey days later had him up nearly 30 points. The final Emerson College poll in late August put Markey at 60 percent to Moulton’s 33 percent. Women and voters under 40 — the exact voters Moulton needed to peel away — broke hardest for Markey, Emerson’s pollster said.

On policy, there was often little daylight between them — a point both men conceded across three debates.

Both called themselves the true progressive in the race and both back universal health care, though not the same version. Markey has embraced Medicare for All, a single-payer system, while Moulton favors a public option that would let a government plan compete alongside private insurers. Markey has also stayed tied to the Green New Deal, which he co-authored.

A major point of contention throughout the race was Moulton’s comments about transgender athletes shortly after President Trump’s 2024 victory, in which he talked about not wanting his daughters “getting run over on a playing field by a male or formerly male athlete.” That prompted an apology from Moulton on the debate stage with Markey, and the incumbent senator accusing the congressman of “throwing trans kids under the bus.”

Markey’s sound win on Tuesday further signals that voters found him to be the unalloyed progressive, with Moulton’s comments around trans issues dogging him throughout the race.

Almost all of Markey’s fellow Massachusetts Democrats in Washington closed ranks, with six of the state’s eight House members and Sen. Elizabeth Warren endorsing him. Only Reps. Stephen Lynch and Jake Auchincloss stayed neutral, The Boston Globe reported.

Moulton’s most notable institutional counterweight came from The Boston Globe, which endorsed him over Markey. He also leaned on fellow veterans-turned-politicians who he helped elect nationally, including New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill.

Throughout the campaign, Markey cited his work with progressive star Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who was a prominent Markey backer against Kennedy in 2020. She held off on endorsing this time before backing him in the race’s final week.

Moulton had unseated an incumbent before, beating then-Rep. John Tierney in 2014. But his recent efforts to crack the party’s upper echelons and comments on trans young people in sports gave Markey’s allies ammunition to paint him as a striver out of step with Massachusetts priorities. In 2018, Moulton waged a failed attempt to block Nancy Pelosi from the speakership, and he made a short-lived 2020 presidential run.

author: EDRi
title: 14 students and opposition politicians targeted by spyware in Serbia
content:
EDRi member SHARE Foundation has confirmed that at least 14 people in Serbia were targeted with advanced spyware since the beginning of 2026 – the largest documented wave of such surveillance in the country to date. Those targeted include members of the student movement, activists, a member of parliament, and a local councilor, all from opposition parties. The timing the of spyware attacks coincides with the local elections held on March 29, 2026.

By SHARE Foundation (guest author) · September 2, 2026

In August 2026, 12 people contacted SHARE’s digital forensics experts after receiving a warning on their phones that they had been targeted in a spyware attack. Apple issues these warnings with high confidence when a user has been targeted by mercenary spyware. SHARE Foundation’s forensic analysis later confirmed two more infections – with a new version of NoviSpy, spyware first discovered in Serbia in 2024. Spyware of this kind can access everything on a device – messages, contacts, photos, app data, and other files – and can secretly record the screen or activate the microphone and camera. Its use is illegal in Serbia.

Two global digital forensics labs – Citizen Lab at the University of Toronto and Amnesty International’s Security Lab – independently confirmed SHARE Foundation’s findings.

Citizen Lab investigators confirmed that the phone belonging to the student movement member who received the warning was infected with Pegasus, a spyware developed by the Israeli company NSO Group. The device was hacked with a zero-click exploit targeting iPhone application iMessage. This means that the device was infected remotely, without any knowledge or interaction by the user.

The remaining 11 devices received Apple Threat Notifications, a high-confidence indicator that they had been targeted with mercenary spyware and should therefore be treated as presumed infected.

“Our forensic findings, and this fresh wave of Apple Threat Notifications reveal that Serbia's peaceful pro-democracy movement is being aggressively targeted with mercenary spyware ahead of key 2026 election cycles."

Amnesty International confirmed the infection with the new version of NoviSpy spyware on the phone of a student movement member whose phone had previously been confiscated when he was brought in for police questioning.

“The forensic findings by SHARE prove that Serbian students continue to be targeted with invasive Android spyware tools, installed while detained by Serbian authorities. The latest 2026 case also reveals a new Android spyware, similar in functionality to NoviSpy, but newly built with specific efforts taken to avoid detection by security experts.”

The same spyware was detected on another device, after private Viber messages from that phone were disclosed live on the Serbian State-aligned TV Informer. Further forensic analysis is ongoing, with support from digital forensics experts at Citizen Lab and Amnesty International.

Intrusive spyware varies by infection method and level of technical sophistication. Pegasus is military-grade spyware, sold exclusively to states and state agencies. It can be installed remotely, with no interaction from the user required, and its key components – the control interface and the servers storing collected data – are typically based in the client country, at the agency’s own premises or headquarters. By contrast, installing the newly discovered spyware requires physical access to the device.

The use of such intrusive technologies represents a gross violation of the right to privacy and heightens the “chilling effect” among citizens, which directly affects related rights such as freedom of expression and movement, as well as a broader range of political freedoms.

The targeting of students, an MP, and a local councilor is especially troubling: political espionage strikes directly at the equality of political actors and the integrity of the electoral process. Democracy depends on elected representatives being free to communicate, organise, and hold those in power to account – without fear of secret, unlawful surveillance. If they aren’t protected from such attacks, other citizens can hardly expect their own privacy and political freedoms to be respected. Practices like this erode trust in institutions, and in the very possibility of free political action.

By its function and purpose, spyware qualifies as a computer virus – that is, a program or set of commands that acts on other programs or data …

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Construction starts on Quaqtaq’s new school
content:
Construction started on Quaqtaq’s new school Wednesday.


Isummasaqvik School

 is expected to be complete in 2030, when it will serve about 250 students from kindergarten through Secondary V, or the final year of high school. It will replace the old school, which operates at its capacity of 125 students, and will have a large gym and space for cultural classes, such as sewing.


Sarah Aloupa, president of the Kativik Ilisarniliriniq school board, hopes the new school will encourage more students to complete high school.


“We have a lot of dropouts at a very young age,” said she said in an interview. “If I could have control, I would let every child graduate.”


Quebec’s Education Ministry approved funding for the project in 2020, and Kativik Ilisarniliriniq awarded the construction contract in January to Les Constructions Pépin et Fortin Inc.


While Wednesday’s groundbreaking ceremony marks the official start of construction, work at the site had already been underway since July, Aloupa said.


Crews have been preparing the foundation, including gravel work and blasting rock. The project provides employment opportunities for locals, with some working at the construction camp and others as heavy equipment operators.


There are plans for the building to connect to the water plant, rather than rely on trucks. School has had to close in the past due to water service disruptions.


However, the provincial funding doesn’t cover the construction of a pipeline, said communications co-ordinator Jade Duchesneau Bernier in an email.


“We are currently working with the Kativik Regional Government and municipal stakeholders to determine how to address this funding gap,” she said.


Once the new school is completed and the existing school is no longer needed, Kativik Ilisarniliriniq plans to renovate the building and convert it into an adult education and vocational centre that serves the Hudson Coast.

author: Andrea DiP
title: Castração química: crueldade de palanque, fracasso de política pública
content:
No último domingo, Flávio Bolsonaro se encontrou com Gustavo Villatoro, ministro da Justiça e Segurança Pública do governo de El Salvador. Após a conversa, que aconteceu em um hotel em São Paulo, o candidato elogiou as políticas de Segurança de Nayib Bukele, que, segundo ele, foi responsável por “implementar um dos maiores e mais eficazes resgates de soberania e devolver a segurança pública para o povo deles”.


Bukele, que se autodenomina “o ditador mais

cool

 do mundo” é hoje um dos ícones da extrema direita punitivista, sendo celebrado por seu governo de Estado de exceção permanente, encarceramento em massa que já levou mais de 100 mil pessoas para as prisões, a suspensão de garantias processuais e violações de direitos humanos que têm sido reiteradamente denunciadas por organizações como a Human Rights Watch e a Anistia Internacional.


Essa “bukelização” da segurança pública –

tema de encontro da Fiesp esta semana

 – é bastante presente nos discursos de Flávio Bolsonaro e em seu plano de governo, intitulado “Brasil sem Medo”. Entre as propostas repetidas aos gritos de “vagabundo” isso, “ladrãozinho” aquilo, pelo candidato em seus palanques, uma se destaca por ser ao mesmo tempo tão simbólica do espírito do tempo como ineficaz e inconstitucional: A castração química para estupradores e pedófilos.


Para começar, é necessário fazer uma diferenciação. A violência sexual contra crianças e adolescentes nem sempre é cometida por um “pedófilo”. Nem todo pedófilo é abusador. E nem todo abusador sexual é um pedófilo.


A pedofilia consta na Classificação Internacional de Doenças e Problemas Relacionados à Saúde (CID) e diz respeito aos transtornos de personalidade causados pela preferência sexual por crianças e adolescentes. O pedófilo não necessariamente pratica o ato de abusar sexualmente de meninos ou meninas. O abusador é quem comete a violência sexual – independentemente de qualquer transtorno de personalidade –, geralmente se aproveitando da relação familiar de proximidade social, ou da vantagem etária e econômica. Por isso, ao contrário do que se pensa, fazer essa diferenciação não significa “passar pano” pra pedófilo. Significa que qualquer um, mesmo sem transtornos de personalidade, pode ser um predador.


O Brasil enfrenta uma epidemia de estupros, como mostrou o último Anuário da Segurança Pública. Foram 87.545 vítimas de estupro e estupro de vulnerável contabilizadas, com cerca de 76% a 78% das vítimas menores de 18 anos ou que se enquadram na definição legal de vulnerabilidade (menores de 14 anos ou pessoas que não podem oferecer consentimento). O Mapa Nacional da Violência de Gênero, que foi divulgado no último dia 25, também traz que quase 29 milhões de mulheres foram vítimas de violência doméstica ou familiar no Brasil nos últimos 12 meses. Quando se fala em violência sexual contra crianças e adolescentes, 64% dos casos de estupro de vulneráveis também são cometidos dentro de casa.


Mas a proposta de Flávio

, requentada da campanha de seu pai e de projetos de lei que tramitam na Câmara e no Senado, e embalada como resposta “firme” contra estupradores

, é, na verdade, uma fraude.


Primeiro porque ela parte da ideia de que a violência sexual nasceria de um impulso masculino descontrolado, de um suposto excesso biológico que poderia ser domesticado por intervenção hormonal.


A castração química nada mais é do que um procedimento que se caracteriza pela manipulação de hormônios que buscam reduzir, temporariamente, o nível de testosterona. Essa redução pode acarretar, entre outros efeitos colaterais, em redução da libido ou da ereção. E, embora adotada em alguns países como pena voluntária ou condicional para liberdade (Como nos Estados Unidos, Coreia do Sul e Polônia) em casos de estupro,

a aplicação e eficácia da medida não possui evidência científica comprovada

 e está longe de ser consenso entre profissionais da saúde e juristas, que consideram a prática uma pena cruel e degradante e que viola a Constituição Federal e a Convenção Americana sobre Direitos Humanos.


Vale lembrar que

a castração química era empregada compulsoriamente contra homossexuais em diversos países da Europa entre os anos de 1940 e 1960, onde a homossexualidade era proibida.

 Um dos casos mais conhecidos foi o do matemático britânico Alan Turing, responsável por decifrar códigos nazistas na Segunda Guerra Mundial, que foi condenado por “indecência grave” em 1952 e submetido ao procedimento, o que contribuiu para o seu …

author: Λουκάς Σταμέλλος
title: «Το κωλόπαιδο ο Μάγγος είναι. Να μη τον δείρουμε;»
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

«Το κωλόπαιδο ο Μάγγος είναι. Να μη τον δείρουμε;»


Η δίκη των έξι αστυνομικών που κατηγορούνται για τον βασανισμό του Βασίλη Μάγγου εντός της Αστυνομικής Διεύθυνσης Μαγνησίας το 2020 συνεχίζεται στο Μικτό Ορκωτό Δικαστήριο της Καρδίτσας. Για αυτόν τον μήνα έχουν προγραμματιστεί δικάσιμοι στις 4, 7, 10 και 17 Σεπτεμβρίου.


Το OmniaTV έχει καλύψει αναλυτικά

τη μέχρι τώρα εξέλιξη της δίκης

 χάρη στη δική σας

στήριξη


Στις δύο τελευταίες δικασίμους πριν από τη θερινή διακοπή, στις 16 και 17 Ιουλίου 2026 στο Μικτό Ορκωτό Δικαστήριο Καρδίτσας, κατέθεσαν συνολικά έξι μάρτυρες.


Στις 16 Ιουλίου εξετάστηκαν οι Δ.Μ. και Θ.Σ. Και οι δύο είχαν δει τον ξυλοδαρμό του Β. Μάγγου έξω από τα δικαστήρια του Βόλου στις 14 Ιουνίου 2020, από διαφορετικές θέσεις. Ο Θ.Σ. μέσα από το όχημα της Ασφάλειας, στο οποίο ήταν κρατούμενος, ενώ ο Δ.Μ. είδε τον ξυλοδαρμό βρισκόμενος στη συγκέντρωση και ήταν, επιπλέον, ένας από τους ανθρώπους που τον παρέλαβαν το απόγευμα έξω από την Αστυνομική Διεύθυνση και τον μετέφεραν με αυτοκίνητο κοντά το σπίτι του.


Στις 17 Ιουλίου κατέθεσαν οι Ε.Ν., Ε.Γ., Λ.Γ. και Γ.Μ. Από αυτούς, ο Γ.Μ. ήταν επίσης αυτόπτης του ξυλοδαρμού έξω από τα δικαστήρια. Οι Ε.Ν., Ε.Γ. και Λ.Γ. κατέθεσαν κυρίως για την εικόνα του Β. Μάγγου πριν και μετά τα γεγονότα, τις συζητήσεις και δημόσιες τοποθετήσεις του τις επόμενες εβδομάδες, καθώς και για την πρόθεσή του να κινηθεί νομικά για όσα είχε υποστεί.


Οι δύο αυτές δικάσιμοι συμπλήρωσαν έτσι τη μέχρι τώρα αποδεικτική διαδικασία με άμεσες μαρτυρίες για τον δημόσιο ξυλοδαρμό, μία ακόμη άμεση μαρτυρία για την κατάσταση στην οποία βρισκόταν ο Β. Μάγγος αμέσως μετά την έξοδό του από την Αστυνομική Διεύθυνση και σειρά καταθέσεων για όσα ο ίδιος περιέγραφε στη συνέχεια, την επιδείνωση της κατάστασής του και τη σαφή βούλησή του να επιδιώξει δικαστική δικαίωση.


Αυτόπτες του ξυλοδαρμού έξω από τα δικαστήρια


Οι τρεις καταθέσεις αυτοπτών του ξυλοδαρμού συγκλίνουν, από διαφορετικές οπτικές γωνίες, στον βασικό πυρήνα των γεγονότων: ο Β. Μάγγος πλησιάζει προς το σημείο όπου βρίσκεται η αστυνομική δύναμη, ένας αστυνομικός με πολιτικά τον υποδεικνύει, αστυνομικοί κινούνται εναντίον του, εκείνος οπισθοχωρεί ή προσπαθεί να προστατευθεί, πέφτει στο έδαφος και δέχεται χτυπήματα ενώ βρίσκεται κάτω.


Ο Δ.Μ. κατέθεσε ότι είδε τον Β. Μάγγο να κάνει βήματα προς τα πίσω και να βάζει τα χέρια στο κεφάλι του για προστασία, πριν δεχθεί γκλοπιές και κλοτσιές. Στην ερώτηση αν αντιστεκόταν, είπε ότι δεν το είδε, γιατί από τη στιγμή που αντιλήφθηκε ότι η υπόλοιπη αστυνομική δύναμη άρχισε να εφορμά και προς το μέρος του, δηλαδή σε όσους βρίσκονταν στη συγκέντρωση έξω από τα δικαστήρια, δικό του μέλημα ήταν να προστατευθεί.


Ο Θ.Σ. έβλεπε το περιστατικό ενώ οι κατηγορούμενοι αστυνομικοί τον μετήγαγαν με όχημα της Ασφάλειας καθώς ήταν κρατούμενος μετά τη σύλληψή του, την προηγούμενη μέρα, στη διαδήλωση κατά της καύσης σκουπιδιών στην ΑΓΕΤ. Κατέθεσε ότι είδε τον Β. Μάγγο να οπισθοχωρεί, άνδρες της ΟΠΚΕ να τον ρίχνουν κάτω και να τον χτυπούν και στη συνέχεια να φτάνει η διμοιρία των ΜΑΤ. Προσδιόρισε ότι είδε σίγουρα τρεις άνδρες της ΟΠΚΕ και έναν των ΜΑΤ να συμμετέχουν στο συγκεκριμένο σκέλος.


Ο Γ.Μ. κατέθεσε ότι ο Β. Μάγγος πλησίασε φωνάζοντας «τι κάνετε ρε», προσπάθησε να καλύψει το πρόσωπό του με τα χέρια και χτυπήθηκε μέχρι που έπεσε κάτω.


«Τι να τον κάνουμε, να μη τον δείρουμε;»


Ο Θ.Σ. κατέθεσε ότι αμέσως μετά το περιστατικό, αφού ξαναμπήκε στο όχημα της Ασφάλειας, ο κατηγορούμενος αστυνομικός Παζαράς είπε:

«

Ο Μάγγος είναι, το μαλακισμένο το κωλόπαιδο. Αυτόν τώρα, τ

ι να τον κάνουμε, να μη τον δείρουμε;»

. Επιβεβαίωσε έτσι την πρόθεση των αστυνομικών να διαπράξουν όσα τους αποδίδονται από το παραπεμπτικό βούλευμα στη συνέχεια, μέσα στο κτίριο της Αστυνομικής Διεύθυνσης Μαγνησίας.


Ο μάρτυρας Δ.Μ. συμπλήρωσε την εικόνα για το τι έγινε μετά την «προσαγωγή», καθώς ήταν και ένας από τους ανθρώπους που παρέλαβαν τον Β. Μάγγο, το ίδιο απόγευμα, «πολύ χτυπημένο», όπως κατέθεσε, λίγο μετά την έξοδό του από την Αστυνομική Διεύθυνση. Τον περιέγραψε άχρωμο και σε πολύ άσχημη κατάσταση, με έντονο πόνο. Κατέθεσε ότι χρειαζόταν βοήθεια για να μπει στο αυτοκίνητο, ζητούσε να πηγαίνουν αργά επειδή πονούσε σε κάθε στροφή ή απότομο φρενάρισμα, κρατούσε τα πλευρά του και είχε τοποθετηθεί σχεδόν ξαπλωμένος. Είπε ακόμη ότι, όταν πέρασαν ξανά από τα δικαστήρια, έτρεμε και ήταν «ράκος».


Ο Δ.Μ. κατέθεσε ότι ο Β. Μάγγος τούς είπε

«τον σάπισαν στο ξύλο»

, ότι άνδρες της ΟΠΚΕ τού κρατούσαν …

author: Marjuice Destinado
title: Cebu activist arrested on National Heroes Day
content:
Cebu-based activist and Makabayan Vice President for Visayas John Ruiz (Contributed photo)

Bayan Central Visayas characterized the incident as a targeted attack on progressive leadership intended to stifle dissent and intimidate grassroots activists.

(1st update) CEBU – The Cebu-based activist and Makabayan Vice President for Visayas John Ruiz was reportedly arrested by elements of the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) on Monday, August 31, shortly after participating in a National Heroes Day protest at the University of the Philippines Cebu.

He posted bail on September 2, according to Karapatan-Central Visayas, and is now temporarily released.

Various sectoral groups gathered on Monday to mark the 75th anniversary of the 1951 US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT). Protesters called for the abrogation of the MDT, the Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA), and the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), asserting that these pacts facilitate a permanent US military presence and unfettered access to Philippine facilities.

Participants also voiced strong opposition to the Philippines’ involvement in Pax Silica, a US-led strategic initiative focusing on cooperation in artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing. Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) Central Visayas warned that the initiative could further expose the nation’s resources, infrastructure, and strategic industries to foreign exploitation.

Read: Why Pax Silica is bad for the Philippines

Throughout the protest, speakers emphasized the need for an independent foreign policy, national industrialization, and a self-reliant defense posture, while denouncing what they described as U.S.-led military intervention and economic exploitation.

The protest concluded at approximately 5:20 p.m. As participants began to disperse, progressive organizations reported that Ruiz was intercepted and taken into custody by alleged CIDG agents.

Civil society groups and progressive organizations across Cebu swiftly condemned the arrest, demanding Ruiz’s immediate release.

Bayan Central Visayas characterized the incident as a targeted attack on progressive leadership intended to stifle dissent and intimidate grassroots activists.

“These attacks expose how state machinery is being used not to defend the interests of the broad masses, but to suppress opposition and protect the interests of the ruling elite,” the group said.

Alyansa sa mga Mamumuo sa Sugbo-Kilusang Mayo Uno (AMA Sugbo-KMU) also denounced the move, highlighting Ruiz’s consistent advocacy for workers’ rights, including campaigns for a living wage and the end of contractualization.

“John Ruiz has stood with workers in pushing for higher wages, regularization, and their rights. AMA SUGBO-KMU condemns this malicious act perpetuated by state forces. We demand for his immediate release,” the labor group said.

Kabataan Partylist Cebu and the League of Filipino Students-Cebu added their voices to the outcry, describing the arrest as a blatant violation of the fundamental right to freedom of expression and assembly.

Advocacy groups pointed to Ruiz’s history of facing legal challenges as evidence of a broader pattern of legal harassment directed at activists.

In December 2023, the Armed Forces of the Philippines filed frustrated homicide charges against Ruiz and fellow activist Jhonggie Rumol. The charges stemmed from a purported armed encounter with the New People’s Army in Toboso, Negros Occidental, in April of that year.

Ruiz has categorically denied the allegations, maintaining he was in Cebu City at the time of the reported encounter. The human rights group Karapatan has labeled the charges as fabricated, asserting they are intended to penalize Ruiz for his opposition to privatization and development projects that displace marginalized communities.

Furthermore, Ruiz is among six individuals charged with violation of Batas Pambansa Blg. 880 (The Public Assembly Act of 1985) following an anti-corruption protest in September 2025. That demonstration, held at the DPWH Cebu City District Engineering Office, demanded transparency regarding flood-control project irregularities. Rights groups maintain this case is yet another attempt to criminalize legitimate political activity.

Ruiz’s arrest occurred amid intensifying state pressure on community leaders and organizations advocating for social justice, raising profound concerns about the diminishing space for democratic engagement in the …

author: Unknown
title: La métropole souhaite nous expulser du bâtiment place de Milan... pour qu'il reste vide
content:
Depuis le 6 mars 2026, nous, les femmes du collectif Solidarités femmes à la rue, occupons un bâtiment car nous n'avions pas d'autres solutions. Le bâtiment est vide et appartient à la métropole. Nous sommes 280 à y avoir trouvé refuge. La métropole nous a collé un procès car il lui était insupportable de voir que son bâtiment inoccupé servait à loger des personnes à la rue. Nous avons tenté de plusieurs fois de les rencontrer, sans succès.


Lors de l'audience, le 12 juin, l'avocat de la métropole a dit que nous devions partir car le bâtiment doit être bientôt détruit pour poursuivre les travaux d'agrandissement de la gare et de rénovation urbaine du quartier.


Et ça, c'est vraiment très urgent, vous comprenez

 

!!!


Héberger les personnes à la rue, ça c'est moins important.


Fin août, le juge a donné raison à la Métropole et demande que le bâtiment de la place de Milan soit évacué «

 

sans délai

 

». 280 personnes dont des femmes et des enfants en bas âge sont menacées d'expulsion dans les prochains jours. Pourtant la Métropole n'a même pas encore demandé le permis de démolir

 

! Cela signifie que cette demande d'expulsion immédiate va laisser le bâtiment vide pendant encore des mois avant sa démolition. La politique de cette métropole est indigne.


C'est pourquoi nous continuerons de lutter contre notre expulsion.


Le collectif solidarités femmes à la rue 69 appelle tous les collectifs, assos, cantines, groupes de potes, groupes de musiques, stars de la danse, artistes en herbe qui le souhaitent à leur envoyer leurs propositions d'événements pour faire vivre la place de Milan ce week-end (5 et 6 septembre) et soutenir les habitantes. Elles cherchent également des banderoles, de préférences grandes (plus grandes que des draps 2 places par ex.) et solides (plastifiées ou bâches).


Pour les contacter, on peut leur écrire sur Instagram ou sur leur adresse mail : solidaritefemmesrue@proton.me

author: Natascha Elena Uhlmann
title: Vermont Hospital Workers Fight for Immigrant Neighbors
content:
Health care workers fighting for a contract in Vermont have come to the table with not only their own demands for safe staffing and fair pay, but also a more unusual demand—one made in solidarity with farmworkers.


They want their employer, the University of Vermont Medical Center, to join the Milk with Dignity program.


“We’ve been in spaces with folks, seen them, heard their stories. They’ve come to our rallies,” said administrative assistant Melissa Lavallee, secretary of the union, Support Staff United (AFT-VT).  “We’re doing for our neighbors what they do for us.”


Milk with Dignity, a framework authored by farmworkers through the local organizing project Migrant Justice, requires affiliated farms to commit to a number of labor standards. It’s modeled off of the Fair Food Program developed by the Coalition of Immokalee Workers, which organizes tomato pickers in Florida.


Farmworkers receive better wages, paid sick time, protection from discipline should they stop performing a task that could put their safety and “serious and immediate danger,” and education on their rights under the agreement.


Migrant Justice notched a big win in 2017 when Ben & Jerry’s—which produces more than 500 pints of ice cream a day in its facility in St. Albans, Vermont—signed an agreement to source dairy from farms that comply with Milk With Dignity’s labor standards. Grocery chain Hannaford has faced years of pressure, but has yet to commit.


Farmworkers and advocates set their sights on the University of Vermont Medical Center for good reason: “Every day, UVM Medical Center serves thousands of patients and workers. It is undoubtedly one of the largest institutional sourcers of dairy in the state,” said Will Lambek, an organizer with Migrant Justice. “By joining Milk with Dignity, the hospital can play a leadership role, inspiring other institutions—including hospitals, schools, and universities—to follow suit,” he said.


Organizers tried to bring the medical center to the table around 2022, but were unsuccessful. “Migrant Justice did not on its own have enough power to take on this important step,” Lambek said. “That’s why it’s so important to have [hospital] workers as allies in this fight.”


“Some don’t understand: ‘What does a farmer’s working conditions have to do with us?’” Lavallee said. “I grew up on a farm in Vermont, and it is the hardest work. Their working conditions are creating our food. Why would we want food created in terrible conditions?”


STRETCHED THIN


Health care workers are stretched thinner than ever. Across the country,

52 hospitals and health systems

 have announced staffing cuts since January. Trump is adding fuel to the fire with his two-pronged assault: Medicaid cuts, and the revocation of work permits for immigrants from countries including Cuba, Haiti, Nicaragua, and Venezuela, many of whom work in health care.


Support Staff United members have been in bargaining for their second contract since April. Among their key priorities is a safe staffing pay differential, to be paid when staffing drops below 80 percent of what is scheduled. They also want to see more paid time off to recover from injuries sustained at work: “My co-workers have been punched in the face. They’ve had ribs fractured. They’ve had fingers broken,” LNA Saer McCillian

told


Vermont Business

.


 Brett Rhodes, a nursing assistant who is now the union’s vice president of organizing, first decided to organize in 2022 after seeing how different things seemed for nurses compared to nursing assistants.


“The nurses had a union. I didn’t really know much about it, I just knew they were getting more respect and more staff,” he said. “When they said something, it had more weight to it. It seemed like they could solve their problems.”


On a typical shift, a nursing assistant must monitor a patient’s heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and body temperature, reposition them to prevent bed sores, monitor their blood sugar and any changes to their mental state, and help them eat and drink. They also shuttle the patient to and from the bathroom safely, and if necessary, clean them up after a bowel movement.


Now try adding nine other patients to the mix. That’s the average load that nursing assistants must attend to in a shift, weaving between rooms and balancing many competing needs.


And the job takes an emotional toll: “Lifting patients is hard,” said Rhodes. “Getting hit by confused patients is hard. But you forget …

author: anred
title: Neuquén: a un año del transfemicidio de Azul Semeñenko, comienza el juicio por jurados
content:
Imagen: Florencia Salto


El 30 de septiembre comenzará el juicio contra Roberto Daniel Sánchez, acusado del asesinato de Azul Semeñenko. La Fiscalía sostiene que se trató de un homicidio triplemente agravado por ensañamiento, violencia de género y odio a la identidad de género. Sus compañeras del Centro de Atención a la Víctima fueron quienes denunciaron su desaparición, sostuvieron la búsqueda y llevaron el reclamo a las calles. Ahora convocan a movilizarse el 25 de septiembre, cuando se cumple un año del crimen y también el cumpleaños de Azul. 

Por Manuela Wilhelm para ANRed.


El 25 de septiembre de 2025, el día en que cumplía años, Azul Semeñenko fue asesinada por un hombre que la contrató para un trabajo sexual. Tenía 49 años, recientemente había iniciado una transición a una identidad como mujer trans y trabajaba como auxiliar en el Centro de Atención a la Víctima (CAV) de Neuquén, un espacio estatal donde se acompañan situaciones de violencia que atraviesan mujeres, travestis y personas trans.


Un año después, su nombre vuelve al centro de la escena: el 30 de septiembre comenzará el juicio por jurados contra Roberto Daniel Sánchez, el hombre acusado por su transfemicidio.


La causa llegará a debate oral con una acusación de homicidio triplemente agravado: por ensañamiento, por haber sido cometido por un hombre contra una mujer mediando violencia de género y por odio a la identidad de género. Si el jurado popular considera acreditado alguno de esos agravantes, la pena prevista es prisión perpetua.


Pero la historia de este caso no comienza con el juicio. Comienza con una desaparición y con un grupo de trabajadoras que se negó a aceptar que esa ausencia pasara inadvertida.


Las compañeras que salieron a buscarla


Verónica Yáñez, psicóloga y compañera de Azul en el CAV, fue quien realizó la denuncia por su desaparición en la Comisaría 16. Azul había desaparecido entre la noche del 24 y la madrugada del 25 de septiembre y no había llegado a un turno que tenía en el Hospital Castro Rendón.


Para sus compañeras había señales que no podían ignorarse. Azul era una trabajadora responsable, y su ausencia no era habitual.


A partir de entonces, las trabajadoras del área comenzaron a reclamar por su búsqueda. No esperaron solamente las respuestas institucionales: salieron a la calle, hicieron intervenciones públicas y comenzaron a instalar el rostro de Azul en distintos puntos de Neuquén.


Una de esas acciones fue un “semaforazo” frente a las oficinas donde trabajaban. Cuando el semáforo se ponía en rojo, las estatales levantaban pancartas con la imagen de Azul y consignas como “No más violencias” y “Basta de matarnos”. Automovilistas y transeúntes respondían con bocinas mientras las trabajadoras insistían en un reclamo elemental: que la desaparición de una mujer trans no quedara naturalizada.


“Es una forma de canalizar el dolor”, explicaban entonces las trabajadoras. También advertían que, aun si el cuerpo encontrado en un canal de desagüe el 14 de octubre no era el de Azul, había una preocupación más profunda: en Neuquén estaban desapareciendo mujeres en situación de vulnerabilidad, como Luciana Muñoz.


La movilización fue creciendo a medida que pasaban los días sin resultados de los rastrillajes policiales en el río Limay.


Las compañeras cuestionaron el modo en que se llevaba adelante la búsqueda y señalaron que no se había activado el protocolo correspondiente desde el área de trata. También reclamaron públicamente la intervención del Estado y denunciaron sentirse abandonadas frente a la desaparición de una compañera de trabajo.


“Nosotras éramos su otra familia”, dijo entonces una de ellas.


Cuando finalmente se confirmó que el cuerpo encontrado en un canal correspondía a Azul, el reclamo cambió de eje pero no se detuvo. Las trabajadoras que habían salido a buscarla comenzaron a exigir justicia y esclarecimiento.


Ese proceso también hizo que el caso adquiriera dimensión pública. El rostro de Azul circuló por las calles, las organizaciones comenzaron a acompañar el reclamo y su desaparición dejó de ser un expediente perdido entre otros.


Hoy, un año después, sus compañeras continúan sosteniendo ese pedido.


Azul, una trabajadora trans


Azul trabajaba como auxiliar en el Centro de Atención a la Víctima. Allí compartía tareas con trabajadoras que acompañaban cotidianamente a personas atravesadas por distintas formas de violencia.


Sus compañeras la recuerdan como una mujer amorosa, solidaria y …

author: Unknown
title: Newroz Ehmed: The autonomy of the YPJ must be preserved
content:
The Women’s Protection Units (YPJ) are insisting on preserving their independent organizational and command structure in negotiations with the Syrian transitional government in Damascus. According to YPJ commander Newroz Ehmed, the Syrian side currently rejects the integration of the organized women’s units into the army. As an alternative, negotiations are underway on integrating the YPJ as intact special units within the internal security forces. “What is crucial for us is that the YPJ preserves its organized structure and autonomy,” Ehmed told the women’s news agency NûJINHA. The YPJ rejects the individual integration of its fighters into existing state structures.


Ehmed was part of the delegation that met in Damascus on 25 August with, among others, self-proclaimed transitional president Ahmed al-Sharaa and Interior Minister Anas Khattab. The talks focused on unresolved issues following the 29 January agreement, including the future of the YPJ, relations between the institutions of the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (DAANES) and Damascus, as well as language and education policy.


Ehmed described the issue of language and education in particular as one of the central points of the negotiations. The talks also addressed military structures and the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), as well as the reconstruction of Syria. Some of the agreed steps, including the dissolution of the SDF as an independent military structure, have since been implemented, while other issues remain unresolved.


“They said the army was not ready for it”


The future of the YPJ has already been the subject of numerous discussions, but no agreement has yet been reached. Ehmed criticized the fact that negotiations concerning the SDF have focused primarily on male-dominated units, while the organized women’s forces have repeatedly been left out. At the most recent meeting, Damascus articulated a clear position for the first time. “We were clearly told that, under the current circumstances, it was not possible to integrate the YPJ into the army. They said that the current Syrian army, and the Syrian government in general, were not yet ready for this.”


The YPJ does not consider this justification convincing. If Syria is being rebuilt, that process must also include the organized women’s forces, Ehmed stated. “We do not have to preserve the structure of the old Syrian army unchanged. Since the beginning of the revolution and the war, social and political conditions have fundamentally changed.”


Special units within the Internal Security Forces


After Damascus rejected the integration of the YPJ into the army, negotiations continued with the Interior Ministry. According to Ehmed, a model is being discussed under which the YPJ could be organized as special units within the internal security structures. However, no final agreement has yet been reached. “What is crucial for us is that we are able to preserve these forces in an organized form,” Ehmed said. The YPJ emerged under wartime conditions, developed over the years, and accumulated extensive military experience, she noted.


The Interior Ministry has stated in principle that women could serve in all areas of the internal security forces. However, the initial proposal envisaged women applying individually and subsequently being assigned to different units. According to Ehmed, this model does not meet the YPJ’s demands. “We want our forces to preserve their existing structure and experience,” she said. The YPJ Command therefore proposed that the women’s units be organized predominantly as intact special units. Representatives of the Interior Ministry responded positively to the proposal.


Independent command structure to be maintained


According to Ehmed, the YPJ currently has more than 1,500 fighters in Kobanê, Hesekê, Qamişlo and Dêrik. The YPJ is demanding that the existing units remain stationed in these regions and be integrated on the basis of their current territorial structure. “For us, it is important to preserve the unity and organized structure of our forces without dissolving them,” Ehmed said. This includes both the women’s units’ shared military experience and their autonomy. Integration must therefore take place “together with their own command structures.”


Ehmed expressed confidence that an agreement could be reached on this model, remarking that joint or state-recognized training structures could also be considered. YPJ fighters, she added …

author: Unknown
title: Tunus’tan Hong Kong’a: İnsan hakları savunucuları hedefte
content:
İnsan Hakları İzleme Örgütü’nün (HRW) bugün yayımladığı raporda, Tunus’ta Cumhurbaşkanı Kays Said yönetiminin son yıllarda sivil topluma yönelik sistematik bir baskı politikası yürüttüğüne yer verdi.


Öte yandan Hong Kong’da demokrasi hareketinin önde gelen isimlerinden Joshua Wong’un “dış güçlerle işbirliği” suçlamasını kabul etmesi ise ifade özgürlüğü ve siyasi örgütlenme hakkı konusundaki tartışmaları yeniden başlattı.


HRW: Tunus’ta sivil toplum tasfiye edilmek isteniyor


HRW’nin “Ödünç Alınmış Zamanda Yaşıyoruz” başlıklı raporunda, Tunus’ta 2021 yılında Cumhurbaşkanı Kays Said’in yetkileri elinde toplamasının ardından demokratik kurumların zayıflatıldığı ve sivil toplum kuruluşlarının hedef haline getirildiği belirtildi.


Rapora göre Mayıs 2024’ten bu yana onlarca sivil toplum çalışanı, insan hakları savunucusu ve dernek yöneticisi hakkında soruşturmalar açıldı. Rapora göre en az 47 kişi sivil toplum faaliyetleri nedeniyle yargılandı, 14 kişi ise hapis cezası aldı. HRW ayrıca çok sayıda derneğin faaliyetlerinin askıya alındığını ve özellikle göçmenler ile mültecilere destek veren kuruluşların kriminalize edildiğini belirtti.


Raporda, hükümetin insan hakları örgütlerini ve bağımsız dernekleri “dış güçlerin aracı” olarak göstermeye çalıştığı, bunun da sivil toplum üzerinde caydırıcı bir etki yarattığı vurgulandı. Rapora göre insan hakları savunucuları, Tunus’ta 2011 devrimi sonrasında elde edilen demokratik kazanımların önemli ölçüde gerilediğini ifade etti.


Hong Kong’da Joshua Wong hakkında yeni dava


Bugün (2 Eylül 2026) Hong Kong Yüksek Mahkemesi’nde görülen davada, demokrasi yanlısı hareketin sembol isimlerinden Joshua Wong, “yabancı kuruluşlarla işbirliği yapma” suçlamasını kabul etti.


BBC’nin haberine göre Wong, 2019 ve 2020 yıllarında uluslararası yaptırım çağrılarıyla bağlantılı faaliyetleri nedeniyle yargılanıyor. Suçlama, Pekin yönetiminin 2020 yılında yürürlüğe koyduğu Ulusal Güvenlik Yasası kapsamında değerlendiriliyor.


29 yaşındaki Wong hâlihazırda başka bir ulusal güvenlik davasından aldığı ceza nedeniyle cezaevinde bulunuyor. Savunması, uzun tutukluluk süresi ve suçlamaları kabul etmiş olmasını gerekçe göstererek daha düşük bir ceza talep etti. Mahkeme henüz karar tarihini açıklamadı.


Uluslararası insan hakları kuruluşları ise Ulusal Güvenlik Yasası’nın Hong Kong’daki siyasi muhalefeti bastırmak için kullanıldığını savunuyor. Pekin ve Hong Kong yönetimi ise yasanın kamu düzeni ve istikrarın korunması açısından gerekli olduğunu ileri sürüyor.


(FY)

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Lianga Massacre and the Lumad struggle
content:
BULATLAT FILE PHOTO. A Sandugo protest in front of Camp Aguinaldo in Quezon City in September 2016 (Photo by Carlo Manalansan/Bulatlat)

More than a decade has passed but justice remains elusive.

CAGAYAN DE ORO — The 2015 Lianga Massacre reflects the continuing struggle of Lumad communities.

The Kalipunan ng Katutubong Mamamayan ng Pilipinas (Katribu), an alliance of Indigenous peoples organizations, stressed this point as various groups commemorated on September 1 the killing of Emerito Samarca, executive director of the Alternative Learning Center for Agricultural and Livelihood Development Incorporated (Alcadev), as well as Lumad leaders Dionel Campos and Datu Juvello Sinzo in Sitio Han-ayan, Barangay Diatagon, Lianga, Surigao del Sur, 11 years ago.

More than a decade has passed but justice remains elusive for the victims of the massacre allegedly perpetrated by paramilitary group Magahat-Bagani with the alleged knowledge of the Philippine military operating in the area.

Read: ‘Soldiers watched as paramilitary attacked us’

Three leaders of Magahat-Bagani were identified as primary suspects, namely Bobby Tejero, Loloy Tejero, and Margarito Layno. Twenty-three other members of the said paramilitary group were also reportedly implicated.

In 2022, one of the Tejero brothers accused of killing the Alcadev executive director was reportedly arrested by authorities. In an Inquirer report, the leader of Magahat-Bagani who allegedly led the September 1, 2015, attack in Lianga, Surigao del Sur, also surrendered to the authorities.

Former Bayan Muna Rep. Eufemia Cullamat who witnessed the incident said that Army officials and personnel allegedly involved should also be held accountable. “It is very clear to us that their killings were due to our efforts to improve our lives and communities while protecting and defending our ancestral lands.”

Cullamat is a cousin of Campos and a niece of Datu Sinzo. She was at the wake of her deceased father when armed paramilitary forces entered the area and ordered them to leave, prompting them to settle in a basketball court. Her cousin Campos was allegedly shot in front of many people.

“Katribu demands accountability for the perpetrators of the Lianga Massacre and all killings of Indigenous Peoples,” the group said in a statement.

Concerned groups said that human rights violations against the Lumad continue despite calls to stop Lumad killings following the bloody 2015 massacre, recounting the killing of Willy Rodriguez, Lenie Rivas, and 12-year-old Angel Rivas—also known as the 2021 Lianga Massacre—who were tagged by the military as members of the New People’s Army (NPA).

They also recalled the case of Lumad youth Obello Bay-ao and Elioterio Ugking who were allegedly killed by members of the Citizen Armed Force Geographical Unit (Cafgu), an auxiliary force of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), in 2017 and 2025, respectively.

In June, Lumad woman Nenita Buscada was killed by members of the Philippine Army’s 88th Infantry Battalion in Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, after they mistook her and her husband as NPA members. The couple reportedly went to a forested area to gather wood and sell it to buy school supplies for their children.

The Lumad struggle for their rights to their ancestral lands also continues, as in the case of the Gulinsao clan that has kept asserting ownership of the land within a government property in Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, as well as the pushback of the Kirinteken-Ilentungen Menuvu against the establishment of a perimeter fence by a banana plantation company within what they claimed as part of their ancestral domain in Don Carlos town, also in Bukidnon.

Katribu said that the repression against the Lumad extends to those who stand with them. The group called for justice for the killing of Lumad school teachers Chad Booc and Gelejurain Ngujo II—part of the New Bataan 5 allegedly massacred in Davao de Oro—and criticized the conviction of former lawmakers Satur Ocampo and France Castro, as well as Lumad volunteer teachers, following their humanitarian mission in 2018 that aimed to rescue Lumad students who allegedly faced harassment by a paramilitary group in Talaingod, Davao del Norte.

Castro said that the 2015 Lianga Massacre is a precursor to the attacks on Lumad schools, of which more than 200 were closed during the Rodrigo Duterte administration, according to the Save Our Schools (SOS) Network, a coalition of various organizations advocating for …

author: Dulce Amor Rodriguez
title: Indigenous communities, advocates launch network opposing Pax Silica
content:
Participants put their signatures signifying their opposition to the Pax Silica Initiative during the launching of the Network Opposed to Pax Silica (NO to Pax Silica) on August 31, 2026. By Dulce Amor Rodriguez/Bulatlat

“We must prioritize the people, not foreign profits.”

MANILA — Indigenous peoples, farmers, scientists, environmental advocates, faith leaders, students, and progressive organizations launched the Network Opposed to Pax Silica (NO to Pax Silica) on Aug. 31, warning that the Marcos, Jr. administration’s participation in the United States-led initiative could threaten ancestral lands, food security, environment, and national sovereignty.

The coalition was launched at the Mary Hill School of Theology in Quezon City amid growing public debate over Pax Silica and the proposed Economic Security Zone (ESZ) in New Clark City, Tarlac.

The network described its formation as the beginning of a nationwide campaign to scrutinize the project and mobilize communities that may be affected by its implementation.

The launch came weeks after government agencies intensified efforts to promote Pax Silica as a flagship industrial and technology initiative linked to artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, and critical minerals under the Luzon Economic Corridor. Government officials said the project could attract billions of dollars in investments and generate more than 130,000 jobs.

The Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) identified a site in New Clark City for what it describes as an AI-native industrial acceleration and manufacturing hub under the Pax Silica framework.

The coalition questioned whether the project would benefit ordinary Filipinos or primarily serve foreign strategic and corporate interests.

“Pax Silica: Development for whom?” became the central question raised throughout the program.

Representatives of Indigenous communities said that they learned about Pax Silica through social media rather than through direct consultations.

Apung Petronila Capiz-Muñoz, chieftain of Sitio Sapang Kawayan in Capas, Tarlac, said that government authorities have yet to explain the project to affected communities.

She also recounted experiences of military red-tagging directed at Indigenous residents who raised concerns about the project.

Capiz-Muñoz said that many Aetas fear the possible loss of ancestral lands and livelihoods.

“How about us Indigenous peoples and fellow farmers?” she asked. “We all know that the land is our life. What will happen to our livelihood?”

She said that the uncertainty surrounding the project deepened anxiety among communities that depend on farming and ancestral lands for survival.

“I cannot accept it,” she said. “I hope Pax Silica will not push through. What will happen to the next generations?”

The coalition said that the proposed Economic Security Zone could affect approximately 1,620 hectares of agricultural and ancestral lands in Capas, Tarlac.

It warned that industrial expansion and land conversion could displace farming families and Indigenous communities while weakening local food production.

Environmental advocates challenged the lack of transparency surrounding the project.

Beauty queen and environmental advocate Beatrice Millan-Windorski said that no publicly available Environmental Impact Assessment has been released for Pax Silica.

“As one of the world’s 18 megabiodiverse countries, we should not bear the brunt of a development with no transparency or clear data on environmental impact,” she said.

Millan-Windorski said that communities deserve access to information before the government proceeds with large-scale industrial projects.

She warned that hyperscale data centers and related infrastructure could place additional pressure on water, energy, and land resources.

“What we do know is that data centers generate a heat island effect and consume immense amounts of energy, water, and resources,” she said.

She also cited reports that farmers in Barangay O’Donnell had been asked to leave lands they had cultivated for generations and warned that hundreds of families could face displacement if the project proceeds.

Antonio Dizon of Ban Toxics raised similar concerns. He warned that the country could become a dumping ground for electronic waste generated by high-technology industries.
